title: Mr. China’s Great Enterprise: Tim Clissold and the Fight for a Chinese Civilisation A-level
summary_zh: 本期节目中，Kaiser Kuo 在北京对话深耕中国近四十年的英国商业调解人、《Mr. China》作者 Tim Clissold，探讨其新书《Teach the People》与耗时二十年的“大业”——在英国高中推动设立全英文授课的“中华文明”A-level课程。Tim 指出，中西方存在严峻的“认知鸿沟”：中国人对西方的了解远超西方对中国，这已成为关乎国家安全与竞争力的结构性短板。两人将当下西方处境与晚清作历史类比，反思西方在能源转型、基础设施与产业政策上的制度掣肘，并探讨如何倒置“中体西用”以实现自我革新。尽管该课程提案获得了英国顶尖高校校长、商界领袖及私人资金支持，却因官僚惰性与单押中文语言教育的误区屡遭英国教育部否决。双方一致认为，无论对华鹰派还是鸽派，打破无知与恐慌、建立透明理性的合作与防御护栏都刻不容缓。
key_takeaways_zh: 中西方存在严重的不对称“认知鸿沟”，中国自改革开放前夕便开始系统性研究西方，而西方对华认知的匮乏正演变为国家安全与战略竞争的致命短板。
当下西方在能源转型、基建效率与全球南方发展合作上正面临类似晚清的“历史大清算”，亟需借鉴冯桂芬式的自省，探索跨越选举周期的长期产业政策与资本引导机制。
英国单纯依赖中文语言教学的策略因母语者升学竞争等结构性障碍导致A-level报考人数减半，仿照“古典文明”设立全英文授课的“中华文明”课程才是扩大对华人才池的可行桥梁。
西方媒体与政界常陷入将中国妖魔化的道德恐慌，而真正理性的对华战略应当跨越鹰鸽分歧，在深刻理解中国运作逻辑的基础上划定透明清晰的合作与防御护栏。

highlights.title_zh: 中西方不对称的“认知鸿沟”
highlights.summary_zh: Tim Clissold 通过江泽民背诵《葛底斯堡演说》、温家宝研读亚当·斯密《道德情操论》以及1977年中国代表团访欧后的震动，论证了中国自上而下对西方的深入了解。相比之下，英国每年仅有300名中国相关专业毕业生，不到兽医专业的三十六分之一，这种认知赤字极易催生非理性的恐惧。
highlights.quote_en: There are 300 graduates a year in Chinese. In veterinary science, there's 36 times more.

highlights.title_zh: 晚清镜像与能源转型主导权易手
highlights.summary_zh: 双方将当前西方与中国的摩擦类比于19世纪中叶的晚清困局，指出贸易逆差、芬太尼危机与制度碰撞等惊人相似之处。Tim 强调，正如蒸汽机与铁路赋予英国百年霸权，下一代电气化能源转型与中国在“全球南方”及“一带一路”倡议中的务实基建输出，正在重塑全球权力格局，而西方却主动放弃了这一主导权。
highlights.quote_en: And we have ceded the next energy transition to China, willfully ceded it.

highlights.title_zh: 冯桂芬之问与西方基建治理困局
highlights.summary_zh: 借用晚清自强运动思想家冯桂芬对体制效能的深刻反思，Tim 呼吁西方从第一性原理审视自身程序民主的执行力危机。他以英国A66公路仅拓宽18英里却需耗时近20年（古罗马修建全线仅用2年）以及年轻一代无法靠劳动积累财富为例，指出西方正面临严峻的现代性交付困境。
highlights.quote_en: What does it mean if procedural democracy can't deliver progress and modernity?

highlights.title_zh: 倒置“体用”与长期产业政策探讨
highlights.summary_zh: Kaiser Kuo 与 Tim 探讨了将晚清“中体西用”倒置为“西体中用”的可能性，即在保留西方个人权利与民主价值的同时，借鉴中国的产业政策与“五年规划”来引导私人资本投向长周期战略领域。Tim 建议英国设立独立于选举周期之外的能源转型与基建常设机构，以保障政策的连续性。
highlights.quote_en: Why is it so terrible to think that you should have an industrial strategy?

highlights.title_zh: “民族”译法之争与对华情绪量表
highlights.summary_zh: Tim 回顾了他与《金融时报》编辑部就“中华民族伟大复兴”中“民族”一词译法的交锋：尽管九本词典和多位汉学家证实应译为 nation，报社仍执意译为带有纳粹色彩的 race，进而引发学者将中国领导人比作希特勒的歇斯底里评论。为此他提出“伍德沃德量表”，主张无论对华鹰派还是鸽派，都必须超越情绪化叙事以增进真实认知。
highlights.quote_en: It doesn't matter where you are on the Woodward scale, we just have to get real about China.

highlights.title_zh: 纯语言教学瓶颈与中华文明课程
highlights.summary_zh: 过去十年英国政府投入2600万英镑推广中文项目，但报考中文A-level的人数反而从3000人跌至1600人，原因在于非母语英国学生在等级考试中无法与华人母语者竞争高分。Tim 主张仿照每年培养6000名毕业生的“古典文明”模式，推出无需中文基础的“中华文明”A-level课程，作为衔接中学兴趣与大学汉学研究的桥梁。
highlights.quote_en: No sensible 16-year-old Brit, non-native speaking Brit, will ever do Mandarin A-level.

highlights.title_zh: 英国教育部的官僚阻力与盲区
highlights.summary_zh: 尽管“中华文明”课程大纲获得了英国最大市值企业董事长、罗素大学集团及十位大学校长的联名支持且无需纳税人资金，却在教育部频繁换帅与官僚推诿中屡屡碰壁。在英国最新发布的272页课程评估报告中，“中国”与“全球化”竟未出现一次，教育部高官甚至否认认知鸿沟的存在。
highlights.quote_en: A top civil servant in the Department for Education doesn't even know that there is a knowledge gap, and that's part of the knowledge gap.

highlights.title_zh: 西方“同文馆”与透明对华护栏
highlights.summary_zh: 引述管仲“百年树人”的名言，Tim 认为扭转对华认知需要内阁办公厅自上而下推动长达数十年的思维转型，建立西方自己的“同文馆”。他指出，一个真正懂中国的英国政府应当告别暗箱操作与跟风禁令（如在缺乏透明解释下封杀华为与明阳智能风电投资），通过公开辩论划定国家安全防御与务实合作的清晰边界。
highlights.quote_en: So, I think we need to set up our own Tongwen Guan.

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Welcome to the Sinica Podcast, a weekly discussion of current affairs in China. In this program, we look at books, ideas, new research, intellectual currents, and cultural trends that can help us better understand what's happening in China's politics, foreign relations, economics, and society.
transcript.zh: 欢迎收听 Sinica Podcast，这是一档聚焦中国时事的每周讨论节目。在本节目中，我们探讨书籍、思想、最新研究、思潮与文化趋势，以帮助大家更透彻地理解中国当下的政治、外交、经济与社会。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Join me each week for in-depth conversations that shed more light and bring less heat to how we think and talk about China. I'm Kaiser Kuo, coming to you this week from Beijing.
transcript.zh: 每周与我一同展开深度对话，为我们思考和讨论中国的方式增添更多洞见，减少情绪化的喧嚣。我是 Kaiser Kuo，本周在北京向大家致意。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Apologies for the long gap between episodes of late. I've been traveling a lot, and it's been really disruptive. Listeners, please support my work by becoming a paying subscriber at sinicapodcast.com.
transcript.zh: 最近两期节目间隔较长，在此深表歉意。近来我一直在频繁出差，工作节奏被打乱得相当厉害。各位听众，若想支持我的工作，请前往 sinicapodcast.com 成为付费订阅会员。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I get how all these Substack subscriptions can really start to add up, and so I try to offer a lot. So in addition to Sinica, you get the Sinica Chinese Phrase of the Week from Andrew Methven. You get podcasts and roundups from the terrific folks at Trivium.
transcript.zh: 我完全理解各种 Substack 订阅费用累积起来确实不少，因此我一直努力为大家提供丰富的权益。除了 Sinica 主节目之外，你还能收到 Andrew Methven 主理的 Sinica 每周中文词汇，以及 Trivium 出色团队制作的播客与资讯综述。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You get my favorite pod, the indispensable China in the Global South Podcast, and you get historian James Carter's This Week in China's History. So please do subscribe so that I can continue to bring you these conversations and lots more.
transcript.zh: 还有我最喜欢的播客——不可或缺的《中国与全球南方播客》（China Global South Podcast），以及历史学者 James Carter 的《中国历史上的这一周》（This Week in China's History）专栏。所以请务必订阅支持，以便我能继续为大家奉上这些精彩对话及更多内容。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: My guest this week, I'm very happy to say, is Tim Clissold. If you read one book about doing business in China back in the 2000s, there's a fair chance that it was his Mr. China, the story of how a young Englishman who ended up as the man in the middle between $400-odd million of Wall Street money and close to 20 Chinese joint ventures that were, to put it gently, not going exactly according to plan.
transcript.zh: 非常高兴地告诉大家，本周的嘉宾是 Tim Clissold。如果你在 2000 年代读过哪怕一本关于在中国做生意的书，很有可能就是他的《中国通》（Mr. China）。书中讲述了一个年轻英国人如何夹在华尔街逾 4 亿美元资金与近 20 家中国合资企业之间——说得委婉点，那些合资项目的发展完全没有按预期推进。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's a very self-aware and admirably self-deprecating tragicomedy that's made many lists of all-time best China books. And though it came out two decades ago, I guess now, people still routinely press it on anyone about to take a job in China, rightly, I think.
transcript.zh: 这是一部极具自省意识、令人称道的自嘲式悲喜剧，曾多次入选各类史上最佳中国题材图书榜单。尽管这本书距今已经出版了二十年，人们仍旧习惯性地把它推荐给任何即将前往中国工作的人——在我看来，这确实理所应当。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He followed it with Chinese Rules, about his adventures in the carbon credit business, and in the years since, he's worked mostly as a mediator, sorting out disputes between Chinese companies and the foreign investors who've fallen out with them. He is a visiting fellow at Jesus College, Cambridge, and he's been living in, working in, and thinking about China for nearly 40 years. But that's not really why he's here today.
transcript.zh: 随后他又出版了《中国规则》（Chinese Rules），讲述自己在碳信用领域的历险经历。在那之后的多年里，他主要从事调解人工作，协助化解中国企业与交恶的外资投资者之间的纠纷。他是剑桥大学耶稣学院的客座研究员，在中国生活、工作并思考中国议题已近 40 年。但这并不是他今天做客节目的主要原因。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: For the past 15 years, Tim has been pursuing what I've taken to calling his Great Enterprise, his dàyè — getting a new A-level in Chinese Civilization into UK schools. For American listeners, A-levels are the exams that 16-to-18-year-olds sit before university. And the idea is actually quite simple: you can study Classical Civilization, Western Civilization in English without a word of Latin or Greek, why not China without the Mandarin?
transcript.zh: 在过去的 15 年里，Tim 一直在致力于推进一项被我称之为他的“大业”（Great Enterprise）的计划——在英国中学引入一门全新的“中国文明”A-level 课程。对美国听众解释一下，A-level 是英国 16 至 18 岁学生在升入大学前参加的高级程度考试。这个构想其实非常简单：既然学生可以用英语研习西方古典文明，哪怕一个拉丁语或希腊语单词都不懂，那为什么不能在不学中文的情况下了解中国呢？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He's assembled a syllabus with a dozen of Britain's leading sinologists. He's lined up 10 vice-chancellors, business leaders, think tanks, and even the money to pay for it all, and he's taken it to the...
transcript.zh: 他联络了十几位英国顶尖的汉学家共同编写了教学大纲。他还争取到了 10 位大学副校长、商界领袖、智库的支持，甚至连全部所需资金都已筹备到位，并将其提交给了……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Department for Education, but so far the answer has been no. The campaign is the focus of his new book, Teach the People: How to Narrow the Knowledge Gap Between China and the West.
transcript.zh: 英国教育部，但迄今为止得到的答复都是否定的。这场奔走呼吁是他新书的核心议题，书名为《训民：如何缩小中西方之间的认知鸿沟》（Teach the People: How to Narrow the Knowledge Gap between China and the West）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And the knowledge gap is its premise. Here's how he puts it: 'The truth is that the Chinese know more about us than we know about them, and that gives them a competitive advantage. The stakes could not be higher, nor the consequences of a mistake more dangerous. For the sake of future generations, we need to close that knowledge gap.'
transcript.zh: 这种“认知鸿沟”正是该书的前提立论。他是这样写的：“事实是，中国人对我们的了解，远多于我们对他们的了解，这赋予了他们竞争优势。形势之严峻无以复加，犯错的后果也再危险不过。为了子孙后代，我们必须填补这一认知鸿沟。”

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: We'll test that premise and then we'll talk about what closing the gap would actually look like. Tim Clissold, welcome at last to Sinica.
transcript.zh: 我们将探讨这一前提，随后深入讨论究竟怎样才能真正缩小这一差距。Tim Clissold，欢迎终于来到 Sinica！

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Thank you, Kaiser.
transcript.zh: 谢谢你，Kaiser。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Tim, you open the book with three scenes, and I'd rather you told them than I paraphrase. There's Jiang Zemin, then the mayor of Shanghai, later of course the president, facing down student protesters back in 1986 who've been quoting Lincoln at him from the Gettysburg Address.
transcript.zh: Tim，你在书的开头描写了三个场景，与其由我转述，不如请你亲自道来。第一个是江泽民，当时他还是上海市长，后来自然成为了国家主席。1986年他直面抗议的学生，而学生们当时正对他背诵林肯的《葛底斯堡演说》。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Then there's Wen Jiabao, premier of course through the 2000s, with a copy of Adam Smith, but not Wealth of Nations. And then there's Xi Jinping on the, you know, the various philosophes of the French Enlightenment who he's proud of saying that he's read. Tell those stories and then tell me why you picked those three in particular to lead the book off.
transcript.zh: 接着是温家宝，他在2000年代担任总理，手边常备一本亚当·斯密的书，却不是《国富论》；再后来是习近平，他自豪地表示自己读过法国启蒙运动的诸位思想家著作。给我们讲讲这些故事吧，并谈谈你为何特意挑出这三幕作为全书的开篇？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So what I tried to do was establish the main premise, which is that there's a huge knowledge gap. So you can do that with all sorts of, you know, anecdotes and meetings and episodes with local government officials or business people or academics.
transcript.zh: 我试图先确立本书的核心前提，那就是双方存在巨大的认知鸿沟。你可以通过各种与地方官员、商界人士或学者的逸事、会面和插曲来证明这一点。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But the one that I chose, which is quite early, because it's absolutely verifiable, was an episode where Jiang Zemin, future, at the time future president of China, he was the mayor of Shanghai and there were student protests and it got quite ugly. There were sort of, you know, smashed shop fronts and all that kind of thing.
transcript.zh: 但我选的这个发生得相当早，而且确凿可考。那是江泽民的经历——未来的中国国家主席，当时他担任上海市长，城里爆发了学生抗议，局势一度相当紧张，出现了沿街商铺被砸这类混乱场面。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. Those were, by the way, the protests that ended up bringing Hu Yaobang out of power. In '87, early...
transcript.zh: 对，顺便提一句，那场抗议最终导致了胡耀邦的下台，是在1987年初……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: No, it was '86. That's true. Yes, so that was that was the Hu Yaobang episode, correct. And then of course, he went back, and then his death sparked the '89 turmoil, yeah.
transcript.zh: 不，是1986年底。没错，那确实是导致胡耀邦去职的事件，对。后来他退了下来，再后来他的逝世引发了1989年的风波，是的。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So anyway, so Jiang Zemin agreed to go and meet with the students to zuo gongzuo, like typical Chinese official, to pacify, listen, try and adjust policy, try and deal with their problems, but it was very touchy.
transcript.zh: 总之，江泽民同意去见学生，就像典型的中国官员那样去“做工作”：安抚情绪、倾听诉求、试图调整政策并化解矛盾，但当时局势非常敏感棘手。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And you know, he arrived at the university quite flustered, not much time to prepare, and he saw scrawled on one of the walls a piece from the Gettysburg Address, you know, 'government of the people, by the people,' and so on.
transcript.zh: 他赶到大学时颇为仓促，没有太多时间做准备。他看到其中一面墙上涂写着《葛底斯堡演说》的名句，也就是“民有、民治、民享”那些话。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And he went into the main auditorium, which is packed, there are about 2,000 students in there, heightened atmosphere, and started discussing with the students. But the key moment when he won them over is he just recited from the top of his head, without notes, in English...
transcript.zh: 他走进了主礼堂，里面黑压压坐了大约两千名学生，气氛剑拔弩张。他开始和学生们对话。但他彻底赢得全场信服的关键时刻，是他完全不看讲稿、仅凭记忆，用英文当场背诵了出来……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: the whole of the Gettysburg Address. And I don't think there are many politicians anywhere that would be able to do that. And I know that that's true because he was — it wasn't a propaganda stunt, because he was challenged to do that later on, on American television.
transcript.zh: 完整背诵《葛底斯堡演说》。我想全世界没几个政客能做到这点。我知道这是真的，绝非宣传噱头，因为后来他在美国电视节目上也接受过这个挑战。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: 60 Minutes, I think.
transcript.zh: 我记得是《60分钟》吧。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, it was, yeah. And he did the same. So that that kind of got me thinking, and you look at other episodes. You know, Wen Jiabao arrives in the UK in something like 2013, and he brings with him a copy of Adam Smith's book, but it's not The Wealth of Nations; it's Theory of Moral Sentiments, which talks about limits that should be placed on the market, and he quoted from it at length to his somewhat bemused hosts.
transcript.zh: 对，就是那档节目。他又背了一遍。这让我陷入了思考，再看看其他例子。温家宝大概在2013年访问英国时，随身带了一本亚当·斯密的名著，但不是《国富论》，而是探讨市场应受约束的《道德情操论》，他还当着略显错愕的英国东道主的面大段引用。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And the first thing he asked was to be taken to Stratford-upon-Avon for a performance of King Lear, where he talked to journalists saying Shakespeare cannot be read once; it cannot be read 10 times. You need to read it 100 times before you can fully understand it.
transcript.zh: 他当时提出的第一个要求，就是去埃文河畔斯特拉特福看一场《李尔王》的演出。他在那里对记者说，莎士比亚的作品读一遍不够，读十遍也不行，要读上一百遍才能真正读懂。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So I think that there's a lot of evidence that the Chinese know much more about Western society, from leadership right down to base levels. So then you start thinking, well, why is that? And I think the reason why it is, is because they had no option.
transcript.zh: 所以我认为大量证据表明，从高层领导到底层民众，中国人对西方社会的了解要深刻得多。这让人不禁思考，为什么会这样？我认为原因在于他们别无选择。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Because in 1977, after Mao died, Hua Guofeng sent a delegation to Europe.
transcript.zh: 因为在1977年毛泽东逝世后，华国锋派出了一个代表团前往欧洲考察。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And they were absolutely flabbergasted. You know, they saw computer-controlled landings at airports, and modern power generation, and high-speed trains. And they just suddenly realized in an instant how far they'd fallen behind.
transcript.zh: 他们彻底惊呆了。他们看到了机场的计算机引导降落、现代化的发电设施以及高速列车。他们瞬间意识到自己落后得有多远。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So when they arrived — it was a month's trip — when they arrived back, they drove straight from the airport to Zhongnanhai, opened a meeting of the Politburo, and they were so excited, the whole meeting continued right throughout the night.
transcript.zh: 考察历时一个月，他们回国后直接从机场驱车前往中南海，召开了中央政治局会议。他们太激动了，整场会议一直持续到通宵。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So they'd suddenly realized in a flash how far they'd fallen behind, and that all these stereotypes about workers being crushed by capitalistic managers wearing top hats and tails, all of that was completely false. So the scales fell from their eyes, and they made it their business to learn about the West.
transcript.zh: 他们刹那间意识到自己被落下了多远，过去宣传中那些工人被头戴大礼帽、身穿燕尾服的资本家残酷压榨的刻板印象，全都不符合现实。他们如梦初醒，并下定决心要把了解西方当成重中之重。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And I think, you know, my basic premise is that we now have an enormous catch-up to do, because the world has changed. And China has come up with a model that is objectively successful on almost all levels, in some way or another, is attractive to other developing countries.
transcript.zh: 我认为我这本书的基本前提是，西方现在面临着极其巨大的认知“补课”任务，因为世界已经变了。中国拿出了一个客观上在几乎所有层面都取得成功的模式，并以某种方式吸引着其他发展中国家。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And we don't really understand how it works. And therefore, because we don't understand it, we can get captured by fear. And that's the last thing we should do. We should learn how to defend ourselves, but also cooperate as well more constructively.
transcript.zh: 而我们根本不了解它是如何运转的。正因如此，出于无知，我们容易被恐惧所绑架。这恰恰是我们最不应该做的。我们应当学会自我防卫，但同时也应进行更具建设性的合作。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So I think the only long-term solution to that is just to raise the body of people in the West who really understand China for what it actually is, warts and all. And we just haven't done that, and we need to. So in the UK...
transcript.zh: 因此我认为唯一的长期解决之道，就是扩大西方内部真正看清中国本质——包括其优势与缺陷——的人群规模。我们过去没有做到这点，而现在必须迎头赶上。在英国……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: There are 300 graduates a year in Chinese. In veterinary science, there's 36 times more.
transcript.zh: 每年中文专业的毕业生只有300人。而兽医专业的毕业生却是这个数字的36倍。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And I know we're a nation of dog lovers, but I still think national security and so on should get a look in. It's just as simple as that.
transcript.zh: 我知道英国是个爱狗成风的国家，但我依然认为国家安全等议题应该受到重视。事情就是这么简单。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. We were talking the other day at lunch, and I warned you that I'd ask this. But there is this familiar pattern in which the smaller, weaker party always knows the bigger one, the stronger one better than the reverse.
transcript.zh: 没错。前几天我们共进午餐时，我提醒过我会问这个问题。通常存在这样一种普遍规律：较小、较弱的一方对较大、较强的一方的了解，总是胜过后者对前者的了解。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Of course, everybody in the world knows America better than America knows them. Chicago knows New York better than New York knows Chicago.
transcript.zh: 当然，全世界对美国的了解都远胜于美国对他们的了解。芝加哥对纽约的了解，也远胜于纽约对芝加哥的了解。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What's your evidence that the China case is something more than the ordinary incuriosity of the bigger party?
transcript.zh: 那你有什么证据表明，中国的情况不仅仅是强势一方惯常的缺乏好奇心呢？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, personally I think, we have to up our game to be able to cooperate and defend ourselves in order to, for society with its values to survive. You know, I mean, the idea of having large-scale, wide conflict with China just doesn't lead anywhere.
transcript.zh: 我个人认为，为了让我们社会的价值观得以维系，我们必须提升自身能力，以便能够既合作又进行自我防卫。与中国发生大规模、广泛的冲突，根本不会带来任何出路。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So you have to find a way of coexisting. And that means understanding China's red lines, pushing where our red lines and their red lines clash, which are not in very large areas. We've got much more in common.
transcript.zh: 所以必须找到一种共存的方式。这就意味着要理解中国的红线，在我们双方红线相撞的领域据理力争——但其实这类领域范围并不大。我们的共同点远多于分歧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It just doesn't feel like very long ago that the obverse was true, that China was the obtuse party here, that it was sort of, it had its head in the sand. It wasn't, you know, learning about the West, and then, you know, until the mid-19th century.
transcript.zh: 但感觉就在不久以前，情况恰恰相反：中国才是迟钝封闭的一方，某种程度上像把头埋在沙子里。直到19世纪中叶之前，中国都没有去主动了解西方。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So what you're essentially saying is that it's flipped, that the whole thing has inverted now?
transcript.zh: 所以你实质上是认为攻守易形了，整个局面现在彻底颠倒过来了？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah. So I think there are tremendous parallels between the current situation and the late Qing.
transcript.zh: 是的。我认为当前的局势与晚清时期有着惊人的相似之处。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I am very fond of those parallels.
transcript.zh: 我向来非常喜欢这种历史类比。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, yeah, and I mean, you mustn't over-egg the kind of repetition of history. Mark Twain says it doesn't repeat itself, but sometimes rhymes. So that's probably about right.
transcript.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我们不能把历史的重复说得太绝对。马克·吐温说过，历史不会重演，但往往押着相同的韵脚。这种说法可能比较贴切。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But if you look at the conflict between the West and China in the mid-1800s, it was basically caused by a trade deficit. So trade deficit is about the most important issue at the moment, particularly with the EU, let alone the US.
transcript.zh: 但如果你审视19世纪中叶西方与中国的冲突，其根源本质上是贸易逆差。而如今贸易逆差也是最核心的问题之一，特别是对欧盟而言，更不用说美国了。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So we've got a trade deficit. Layer on top of that an opium crisis, so the opium crisis in the US, which the US claims is being facilitated by China. And then enormous technology catch-up, clash of systems, mutual misunderstanding, all sorts of different parallels.
transcript.zh: 因此我们面临着贸易逆差。在此之上还叠加了鸦片危机——美国本土的类鸦片芬太尼危机，美方声称中国在其中起到了推波助澜的作用。此外还有巨大的技术追赶、体制冲突、彼此误解，各种层面都有相似之处。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: You know, on the one side, you have a hectic, undisciplined leader who is tolerant of misbehavior by his underlings. And on the other side, in China, you have an incredibly highly disciplined administrative and bureaucratic structure headed by...
transcript.zh: 你看，一方面，我们有一个行事忙乱、缺乏纪律、纵容下属不轨行为的领导人；而另一方面，在中国，则拥有一套纪律极其严明的行政与官僚体制，其掌舵者……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: ...a highly competent set of technocrats who face no election. Well, I mean, you just flip it back over, that, you know, you've got Qianlong and everything that was going on, corruption, and so on, there. So, yeah, Heshen, yeah.
transcript.zh: ……一群能力极强、无需面对选举的技术官僚。但反过来看，当年有乾隆，还有那时的腐败等等。所以，对，还有和珅，确实。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, I think the situation is reversed, and it's accelerating. I mean, you explained it, I thought, incredibly lucidly in your essay The Great Reckoning.
transcript.zh: 因此，我认为攻守之势已经逆转，而且这一进程还在加速。你在那篇《大清算》（The Great Reckoning）的文章里，对此阐述得极其透彻。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, thank you.
transcript.zh: 谢谢。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, what does the West do when it is no longer driving modernity? What does that mean? What does it mean when we can see a system that is objectively delivering greater benefits and happiness to its populace than than ours is?
transcript.zh: 那么，当西方不再主导现代性时，西方该何去何从？这意味着什么？当我们眼睁睁看着另一种体制客观上为其民众带来的福祉与幸福感超越了我们自身时，这又意味着什么？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: What does that mean for our system? We have to start rethinking how we compete and how we strengthen ourselves. I'd certainly go as far as to say that we should study the reaction of the Qing intellectuals to this predicament, and we should study what they did to see if there's anything we can learn from looking back, and then adapting it to the current situation.
transcript.zh: 这对我们的体制意味着什么？我们必须重新思考该如何竞争，如何自强。我完全可以说，我们应当去研究晚清知识分子在面对这一困局时的反应，去研究他们的所作所为，看看能否借古鉴今，并将其运用于当下的局势。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And indeed, that's what you do. Yeah.
transcript.zh: 而这正是你在书中所做的，对。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Again, I don't want to overegg this comparison between late Qing and where we are now. I think that the gap is going to widen. There are signs of it already widening in a catastrophic way in automotive, pharmaceuticals...
transcript.zh: 同样，我不想过度拔高晚清与我们当下处境的类比。但这种差距确实正在拉大。在汽车、生物制药等领域，已经出现了差距呈灾难性扩大的迹象……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Green energy, of course.
transcript.zh: 当然还有绿色能源。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Energy transition is absolutely critical. I actually happen to come from a little village in the north of England where the promoters' meeting of the Stockton and Darlington Railway was held in an upstairs room in a pub. That was the first passenger railway in the world.
transcript.zh: 能源转型是绝对的重中之重。我碰巧来自英格兰北部的一个小村庄，当年斯托克顿和达灵顿铁路的发起人会议就是在当地一家酒吧的楼上房间举行的。那是世界上第一条客运铁路。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So that was, in a sense, the culmination of the transition from water power to fossil fuel. Look what that did to Britain. It gave it a century of dominance.
transcript.zh: 从某种意义上说，那是从水力转向化石燃料这一进程的巅峰。看看这给英国带来了什么——整整一个世纪的霸权。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And we have ceded the next energy transition to China, willfully ceded it. We're now led by a man who stood up in the last couple of weeks in front of the United Nations General Assembly and described climate change as the greatest con job in human history.
transcript.zh: 而如今，我们却把下一轮能源转型的先机拱手让给了中国，几乎是任性地放弃了。就在过去几周里，我们的领导人还站在联合国大会上，公然宣称气候变化是人类历史上最大的骗局。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, what do we do? It's got nothing to do with politics. It's cheaper. It's cheaper, and it gives people greater independence.
transcript.zh: 那我们该怎么办？这根本与政治无关。它成本更低，不仅更便宜，还能赋予人们更大的自主权。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: China did not embark on this journey to electrify because of some concern about climate change. It did it to get energy independence, and because the population was worried about pollution. So purely pragmatic, practical reasons.
transcript.zh: 中国开启电气化之路，并不是出于对气候变化的什么崇高关切，而是为了实现能源独立，并且因为老百姓对环境污染怨声载道。完全是出于务实、现实的考量。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's right. So, I mean, the historical frame of a good section of the book is the decade of the 1860s, after the Second Opium War, British and French troops, the Anglo-French troops...
transcript.zh: 没错。你书中很大一部分的历史参照系是19世纪60年代，第二次鸦片战争之后，英法联军……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Looted the Old Summer Palace, the Yuanmingyuan, it was no longer possible for China's rulers to pretend that nothing fundamental had changed, right? You pretty much say that the West is at that point now.
transcript.zh: 劫掠了圆明园之后，统治者就再也无法假装一切根本没变了，对吧？你基本认为西方现在也走到了这一步。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, unpack the historical analogy a little bit more. I know we don't want, as you say, to overegg it, but what was our Second Opium War? When did pretending stop being possible? Was there a moment?
transcript.zh: 那么，请进一步剖析一下这个历史类比。我知道正如你所说，我们不想言过其实，但西方的‘第二次鸦片战争’是什么？假装无事从何时起变得不再可能？是否存在某个标志性时刻？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, I think after the catastrophic defeat, I mean after the First Opium War, which was 1839, Treaty of Nanjing I think was 1842, but let's not worry about that. That ceded the island of Hong Kong in perpetuity, but it was a relative skirmish.
transcript.zh: 我认为是在那场灾难性的溃败之后。我是指，第一次鸦片战争始于1839年，《南京条约》大概是1842年签订的，不过这先按下不表。那次条约永久割让了香港岛，但那在当时相对只是一场边境冲突。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: It didn't affect the capital. It didn't affect the north so much. It was going on roughly the same time as the Taiping and other rebellions, so it was just one of these enormous headaches.
transcript.zh: 它没有波及京城，对北方的影响也没那么大。当时正值太平天国等叛乱频发，因此它只是朝廷众多心腹大患中的一个。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: The Second Opium War was profoundly different because it came to the capital. The Summer Palace was wrecked, and the emperor fled. There was no longer any possibility of trying to pretend that this is just another skirmish that the system will be able to put down.
transcript.zh: 第二次鸦片战争则有着根本的不同，因为敌军直接打到了京城。圆明园被焚毁，皇帝仓皇出逃。至此，统治者再无可能假装这只是一场体制自身能够平息的局部冲突了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What's the analogy here in the West today?
transcript.zh: 那今天西方的类似处境是什么？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, I think the energy transition is probably the most important thing. Energy transition plus development, so what I mean by that is China sort of set itself up as the shop steward of the Global South.
transcript.zh: 我认为，能源转型可能是最核心的因素。能源转型加上发展议题，我的意思是，中国在某种程度上将自己定位成了‘全球南方’的工会首席代表。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And that's where all the development and economic growth is going to take place over the next 30 years. So, you know, Belt and Road Initiative, enormously important. And the West had decades to try to assist and so on with the developing world.
transcript.zh: 而未来三十年所有的发展与经济增长都将集中在这些地区。因此，“一带一路”倡议极其重要。西方原本有数十年的时间去向发展中国家提供援助与合作。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: One of the little anecdotes is that Larry Summers went to Kenya, I think it was Kenya, and met someone in the president's office and they said to him, 'When America comes, we get a lecture. When China comes, we get an airport.'
transcript.zh: 有个广为流传的小轶事：Larry Summers 访问肯尼亚——我记得是肯尼亚，在总统办公室见到了某位官员，对方对他说：‘美国人来时，我们受到一通说教；中国人来时，我们得到一座机场。’

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So the development path that China offers the Global South is very different from the one that was offered by the West, and people find it attractive. So you've got energy transition plus this enormous shift of wealth and power from the West to other places.
transcript.zh: 因此，中国为全球南方提供的发展路径，与西方当年提供的截然不同，而且人们觉得它颇具吸引力。所以，一边是能源转型，另一边则是财富和权力从西方大规模转移到其他地区。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: It's coupled with what I think is going to be an absolute technology revolution that the West is not really leading anymore. You get transition to electric vehicles, renewables, pharma.
transcript.zh: 更重要的是，这还伴随着一场西方面临彻底失势的技术革命。从新能源汽车的转型，到可再生能源，再到生物医药。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, so it's not one gigantic shock, right?
transcript.zh: 对，所以这并不是单一一次巨大的震荡，是吧？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: No, it's a gigantic shock, and it's going to be an intellectual shock because we're going to have to say, 'Well, how could that possibly have happened?'
transcript.zh: 不，它依然是一场巨大冲击，而且将是一场智识层面的震撼，因为我们不得不自问：‘这一切究竟是怎么发生的？’

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That may be the problem actually. It's weird how we seem only to respond in the face of...
transcript.zh: 这其实可能正是问题所在。奇怪的是，我们似乎只有在面对……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Cataclysm, right. And we I don't want to catastrophize China and it's not. It's a good thing, but yeah, there hasn't been one event that's proved to be, you know, sort of the forcing function, right?
transcript.zh: 没错，一场灾难。我不想把中国的前景灾难化，事实也并非如此，这是件好事，但确实还没有出现哪单一事件能成为那种倒逼变革的催化剂。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But what happens, so Huawei is now, you know, developing a completely different approach, in tandem with some others, there are other Western companies that are also doing it, but they're basically developing a completely new approach to semiconductors.
transcript.zh: 但如果换个情况呢，比如华为现在正在与其他一些企业联手探索一种完全不同的路径，西方也有一些公司在做，但他们基本上是在为半导体开辟一条全新的进路。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, to make them faster not by... Not by node size, right?
transcript.zh: 对，提高运行速度而不是靠……缩小制程节点，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, make them faster, exactly, not by node size. So what happens if that's successful? What does that do to the whole way that we think, let alone who can dominate the infotech business?
transcript.zh: 对，提高速度，完全正确，而不是靠缩小制程。如果这成功了会怎样？这会对我们的整个思维方式产生什么冲击，更不用说谁将主导信息技术产业了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right, right. Your story about Larry Summers has a Twitter equivalent that I saw last year, and I was hysterical. Somebody had written, you know, that that old line, I think it was a Kenyan person who had said, "When the Chinese come to town, we get a hospital. When the Americans come, we get a lecture."
transcript.zh: 没错，确实。你提到 Larry Summers 的故事，我去年在 Twitter 上也看过一个类似的段子，简直笑死我了。有人写了那句老话，好像是个肯尼亚人说的：‘中国人来的时候，我们得到一座医院；美国人来的时候，我们换来一顿说教。’

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: To which some American had replied, "Don't don't assume that that hospital comes with no strings attached." And then the Kenyan wrote, "Here comes the lecture."
transcript.zh: 结果有个美国人回复说：‘别以为那座医院是不带任何附加条件的。’接着那个肯尼亚人回了一句：‘瞧，说教这不就来了。’

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Exactly! Exactly, very good.
transcript.zh: 精辟！太精辟了，非常绝。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, the rapidity with which that response came in was genius too. Anyway, the hero of that section, when I said you talk about the intellectual response in China, is Feng Guifen, who was a scholar-official from Suzhou, writing in Shanghai in 1861.
transcript.zh: 没错，那个回复接得之快也堪称神来之笔。言归正传，书里讲到中国知识分子的回应时，那个章节的主人公是冯桂芬，一位来自苏州的士大夫，1861年在上海撰文著书。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He was a major figure of what we've come to call the Self-Strengthening Movement, and he asked why Western nations were small and strong, while China was vast and weak. And he came up with four respects in which China really fell short, and you go through these.
transcript.zh: 他是我们如今所称的‘洋务运动’（自强运动）的重要人物，他质问为什么西方列强虽小却强，而中国版图辽阔却积弱不振。他总结了中国确实落后的四个方面，你在书中也逐一梳理了这些。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You propose that the West now ask the reciprocal questions. What are they, and which one is the hardest for us to ask honestly?
transcript.zh: 你提议西方现在应该提出对等的反躬自问。这些问题是什么？对我们来说，最难诚实面对的是哪一个？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, Feng Guifen had talked about full use of human talent, and full benefit from the land, and ruler and people not in estrangement, and names matching realities. None of these seem like the sorts of things that are going to stimulate a lot of... But what are the questions that should be driving us?
transcript.zh: 冯桂芬当时谈的是‘人无弃才’、‘地无弃利’、‘君民不隔’、‘名实相符’。这些听起来似乎都不像是能激起大量……但究竟哪些问题才应当驱动我们去反思？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, it's I think it's much more basic, which is, that what does it mean for us when our government is not really empowered to make change, because there are so many constraints on it? What does it mean if procedural democracy can't deliver progress and modernity?
transcript.zh: 我认为问题其实更为根本：当我们的政府受到重重制约、根本没有实权去推行变革时，这对我们意味着什么？如果程序性民主无法带来进步与现代化，这又意味着什么？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: It's as basic as that. So we need to start right from the beginning, which is what Feng Guifen tried to do. As you know, there's a collection of 47 essays that he wrote.
transcript.zh: 道理就这么简单。所以我们需要追根溯源，而这也正是冯桂芬当年试图做的事。如你所知，他写过包含47篇文章的文集（《校邠庐抗议》）。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: After he came into contact with Westerners, so he'd been a very traditional Confucian scholar, came from a long line of scholar-officials based in Suzhou.
transcript.zh: 在他接触西方人之后……他原本是个非常传统的儒家学者，出身于苏州世代相传的士大夫家族。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: He passed the provincial exams with flying colors, went to Beijing, failed two times I think, but eventually became the number two I think in the imperial exams. And then, he was assigned to the Hanlin Academy, and then he went back down to Suzhou and did tax reform and government. So he's a very upright, austere, moral, Confucian scholar-official.
transcript.zh: 他以优异成绩考中乡试，之后进京赶考，好像落第了两次，但最终在殿试中考中了榜眼。随后他被点入翰林院，之后又回到苏州主持税制改革和地方政务。所以他是一位非常刚正、清简、注重道德操守的儒家士大夫。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And then the Taiping Rebellion hit, and he had to flee from Suzhou and took refuge in Shanghai. And then he was forced to observe the foreigners and all the things that they had that China hadn't. So he asked the really, really basic questions, which is: why is the Confucian system superior if it can't perform?
transcript.zh: 后来太平天国起义爆发，他不得不逃离苏州，到上海避难。在那里，他不得不近距离观察洋人以及他们拥有而中国所匮乏的一切事物。于是他提出了极其根本的问题：如果儒家体系无法经世致用，它何谈优越？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And there were lots of themes in his essays, including how we deal with foreigners, and that's the one I focus on.
transcript.zh: 他的文集中探讨了诸多主题，包括如何应对夷人，这也是我所关注的重点。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Tim, you told me just now that it hasn't actually ever been translated into English, which is bizarre to me.
transcript.zh: Tim，你刚才跟我说，这本书居然从来没有被完整翻译成英文，这让我感到匪夷所思。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: That's right. So, it's bizarre. It's been translated into, well not completely translated, into German. There is a PhD done in 1968 in the US, and I actually went over to see the guy that wrote it and, unfortunately, he'd forgotten almost everything about it. But it's very, very kind of understudied.
transcript.zh: 没错。确实很不可思议。它曾被翻译成德文，不过也不是全译本。美国在1968年有一篇相关的博士论文，我甚至还专门跑去拜访了那位作者，可惜他基本上已经把当年的研究忘得一干二净了。所以这方面的研究非常欠缺。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, yeah, so I mean I just used AI to translate, it's fantastic. So, basically that means I can read it quickly, and then if there are really core parts, then I go back to the original and drill down and try and understand it.
transcript.zh: 所以我就直接用AI来翻译，效果非常棒。基本上我可以用它快速通读，一旦遇到真正核心的段落，我就回过头去看原文，深入推敲以求彻底理解。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Right. But I mean to me it's extraordinary that it's never been translated, because it is, it's very thought-provoking. We need to do the same kind of self-introspective soul-searching, ask ourselves these very basic questions.
transcript.zh: 对。但对我而言，它从未被翻译成英文确实很不可思议，因为它非常发人深省。我们西方现在也需要进行同样的内省与灵魂拷问，问问自己那些最根本的问题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It sounds like you're asking us to do it all from first principles here. If our procedural democracy somehow is...
transcript.zh: 听起来你是在要求我们从第一性原理出发去重新审视一切。如果我们的程序性民主在某种程度上……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah. And I'm quite sure if we did go back, then we'd find lots of things that are fantastic about our system, you know, a high set of civil rights, all these things. But there is, there's a problem.
transcript.zh: 是的。而且我十分确信，如果我们真去溯本求源，会发现我们体系中有很多极好的东西，比如高度保障的公民权利等等。但问题确实存在。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, I live in North Yorkshire, near Scotch Corner. And there's a road that traverses the UK in the north, called the A66, and it goes from the east coast to the west coast, and it was built in Roman times.
transcript.zh: 比如，我住在北约克郡的斯考奇角附近。英格兰北部有一条横贯东西海岸的公路，叫做A66公路，它最早在罗马时代就修建了。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: It's 50 miles long, and 18 miles of it are single carriageway, but it's an absolutely crucial trunk road across the country. So the government in 2017 decided that they would make the whole thing a dual carriageway.
transcript.zh: 这条路全长50英里，其中有18英里仍是单车道，但它绝对是一条横贯全国的关键干道。于是英国政府在2017年决定，将整条路拓宽为双车道。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: years already, no work has started. So at the moment the projection is that it may be finished by 2035. This is 18 miles, just widening a road.
transcript.zh: 都过去好几年了，工程还没动工。目前预计可能要到2035年才能完工。这只是区区18英里的道路拓宽工程。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So that's something... and it won't be finished then, so it will probably be around 20 years to widen it over 18 miles. So it's not completely conclusive, but archaeological evidence says that the Romans built that road in two years.
transcript.zh: 到时候恐怕也完不成，所以拓宽这18英里大概得花20年左右。虽然还不算板上钉钉，但考古证据显示，当年罗马人修这条路只用了两年。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, and that was done in between AD 79 and 81.
transcript.zh: 那还是在公元79年到81年之间建成的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Two months would be long for China, right?
transcript.zh: 这要是放在中国，两个月都算慢的了吧？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah. So something, something's gone wrong, you know, when people are, you know, terribly concerned about cost of living, and yet they see, you know, Gini coefficients going up and enormous wealth of, you know, capital accretion. Er, you know, um, I think there's a extra million people around 30 in the UK who are now living at home because they can't afford um, yeah, their own housing.
transcript.zh: 是啊。所以肯定是哪里出问题了。人们一方面对生活成本焦虑万分，另一方面却目睹基尼系数攀升和资本积累带来的巨额财富。在英国，30岁左右买不起房只能窝在家里和父母挤在一起的年轻人，恐怕又多了上百万。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I mean, it's the truth. My son said to me the other day, you know, his generation cannot create wealth, cannot generate wealth by working. Yeah, they can't, they can't do that by, in the way that, you know, in the '60s, '70s, '80s people could, just with a job, and saving, and property, and so on.
transcript.zh: 事实确实如此。前几天我儿子对我说，他们这一代人根本无法仅靠工作来创造财富、积累财富。他们完全无法像六七十年代乃至八十年代的人那样，靠一份普通工作、攒钱买房等方式来实现财富积累。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, so I think we've got a lot of thinking to do. And I definitely don't have the all, all the answers, but I want to try to orchestrate some way that there's a forum where we can grapple with these really deep problems. Because otherwise we're just sort of sleepwalking into what the Qing Dynasty did.
transcript.zh: 所以我觉得我们有太多需要反思的地方。我当然没有全部答案，但我想设法促成某种对话平台，让我们能正视这些极其深刻的难题。否则，我们就是在浑浑噩噩中重蹈大清帝国的覆辙。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, but let let's be clear. You say that you don't have all the answers, but neither do you say that China has all the answers, right? That's, I've just, just lest anyone think that that's it.
transcript.zh: 对，但我们得先澄清一点：你说你没有全部答案，但你同样没有宣称中国就掌握了所有答案，对吧？我只是想防患于未然，免得有人往那方面去想。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: No, and China is absolutely explicit by saying that it cannot, you know, its system can't be just spliced onto, you know, just put onto another system. So no, we we have to find our own solutions, um, you know, which are based on our own heritage.
transcript.zh: 绝非如此。中国自己也明确表示，其制度不能生搬硬套、直接嫁接移植到其他制度之上。所以我们必须扎根于自身的文化遗产，去探寻属于自己的解决方案。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And I just think, you know, our own heritage to to a degree has been captured by the current zeitgeist. And you know, if you look at Hobbes, Leviathan, then it's remarkably similar to what, you know, the Party would say say it say in China.
transcript.zh: 而且我觉得，我们在某种程度上被当下的时代思潮给禁锢了。如果你回看霍布斯的《利维坦》，就会发现其中的很多论述与中共在中国的执政话语惊人地相似。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So so there are all sorts of strands of thought in Western philosophy, you know, which are which have just been sort of like cut off, I think. And we need to, we can look back into our own rich philosophical world of thought to find the answers, to just use China as a reference, which is exactly what the Chinese did, you know, is uh, use use the Chinese as the main body. Zhongxue wei ti, waixue wei yong.
transcript.zh: 西方哲学里本有诸多思想脉络，如今却几乎被我们一刀切地弃之不顾了。我们完全可以回溯自身丰饶的哲学思想宝库去寻找答案，仅仅把中国作为一个参照系——正如中国人当年所做的那样：以自身为主体，“中学为体，西学为用”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. This ti-yong formula, you know, this is this is sort of the the foreshortening of of all of Feng Guifen's ideas: Chinese learning as the essence, Western learning for practical use. That's right. You're sort of proposing the inversion here? That's something I've observed might in fact be happening now: Western values as the essence, the the privacy and...
transcript.zh: 没错。这个“体用”公式，可以说是冯桂芬思想精髓的高度概括：即“以中国伦常名教为原本，辅以诸国富强之术”。而你在这里其实提出了一种倒置？这也正是我观察到的现状：以西方价值观为体，将隐私与个人权利视为根本……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...sovereignty of the individual, procedural democracy, all the good stuff, but with Chinese methods for use, right? The yòng is industrial policy, actually making stuff, all, you know, what China is doing.
transcript.zh: ……个体主权、程序民主等所有这些优秀内核，但以中国方法为‘用’。这里的‘用’指的是产业政策、实体制造，也就是中国当下正在做的事情。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The original, though, didn't survive contact with reality, right? The methods turned out to be inseparable from the institutions that produced them, right? So the yòng is not separable from the tǐ.
transcript.zh: 但当年的‘中体西用’终究没能经受住现实的检验，对吧？事实证明，方法根本无法脱离孕育它们的制度。也就是说，‘用’与‘体’是无法割裂的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I wonder if the inverted version has the same problem. I mean, can you have the electro-state that China now has without the party-state?
transcript.zh: 我想知道反过来的‘西体中用’是否也会面临同样的问题。我的意思是，如果没有党国体制，你能拥有中国如今这种‘电气化国家’吗？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, I mean, that's a fundamental question, isn't it? So it's whether, you know, can you have—can you, for example, can we, within a parliamentary democracy within an election cycle, can we create bodies that survive the electoral cycle to deal with problems that are on a very long-term scale?
transcript.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一个根本性的问题，不是吗？关键在于，我们能否在议会民主和选举周期的框架内，建立起超越选举周期存续的机构，去应对那些时间跨度极长的深层次问题？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Sounds like you're talking about the deep state there, mister.
transcript.zh: 先生，听起来你像是在讨论‘深层政府’（Deep State）啊。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, exactly. That's part of the whole debate, but the UK set up the Office for Budget Responsibility, which holds successive governments to account.
transcript.zh: 确实如此，这本身就是整场辩论的一部分。但英国也设立了预算责任办公室（OBR），用来问责历届政府。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So I just want to debate, do we need an office for energy transition? Do we need an office for infrastructure that survives the endless, repetitive cycle where public opinion just changes and then the government changes?
transcript.zh: 所以我只想探讨一下：我们是否需要一个能源转型办公室？我们是否需要一个基础设施办公室？让它们能够超越那种民意一变、政府跟着倒台的无休止恶性循环？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: You can't plan a business unless you have stability in a policy framework. Why is it so terrible to think that you should have an industrial strategy?
transcript.zh: 如果政策框架缺乏稳定性，企业根本无法做长远规划。认为国家理应制定产业战略，这种想法难道就很可怕吗？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: We can learn a lot from the way that the Chinese have orchestrated private capital. Personally, when I was on the investment side before I started doing dispute resolution, my playbook was the Five-Year Plan.
transcript.zh: 在调配和引导民间资本方面，我们完全可以向中国借鉴很多经验。就我个人而言，在我转型做纠纷调解之前从事投资时，我的‘行动指南’就是五年规划。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Because if your business in China was coterminous and helped to implement the Five-Year Plan, you had a huge tailwind behind you.
transcript.zh: 因为如果你的在华业务与‘五年规划’方向一致并助力其落实，你就会获得巨大的政策顺风。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's right. You get free phone calls, right? They'll tell you, 'This is where we're going to clear all the regulatory hurdles for you. This is where we're going to be giving you money and tax policy that...' Exactly.
transcript.zh: 没错。你会一路绿灯，他们会直接告诉你：‘我们会帮你扫清所有监管障碍，我们会为你提供资金支持以及优惠的税收政策……’确实如此。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: David Fishman and I—I don't know if you know who he is, but he's an energy consultant based out of Shanghai, a brilliant guy—he and I co-wrote a paper for this publication, a fairly new publication called The Breakthrough, in which we basically argued that the kind of energy transition that we've seen happen in China isn't really possible under the capitalism that we have in the West right now...
transcript.zh: 我和 David Fishman——我不知道你是否认识他，他是常驻上海的能源咨询顾问，非常优秀的一个人——我们曾为一家名为《The Breakthrough》的新刊物合写过一篇文章。我们在文中的核心论点是：我们当前在西方实行的这种资本主义模式，根本不可能实现我们在中国看到的那种能源转型……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...that doesn't nail the investors' feet to the floor, that allows them to flee when the time horizons are too long and when the returns...
transcript.zh: ……因为现行制度无法把投资者的双脚牢牢钉在地面上，一旦投资回报周期过长、预期收益不稳，资本就会迅速撤离跑路……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Are too small. But, you know, look what's happened in China in things like polysilicon versus, say, Northvolt in Scandinavia, where private money fled because it could, because the horizon in spite of having some $30 billion in pre-sales already, it was just...
transcript.zh: 规模太小了。但你看，中国在多晶硅等领域的发展，对比一下斯堪的纳维亚的Northvolt电池公司，那里的私人资本说撤就撤，因为它们有退路，哪怕手握约300亿美元的预售订单，可投资回报周期太长，资金还是撤了……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: No, that's right. That's exactly right. So that, that's just one area where we should be debating. You know, how do we marshal capital into the areas which are really structural for the next generation?
transcript.zh: 没错，一点都没错。这恰恰是我们应该深入探讨的领域之一。我们究竟该如何引导和调动资本，投向那些关乎下一代生计的真正具有结构性意义的领域？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And I mean, you ask in your essay, The Great Reckoning, you know, if, if a democratic system can't protect the very habitability of the planet, you know, why is it superior?
transcript.zh: 你在《大清算》（The Great Reckoning）那篇文章里也质问过：如果一个民主体制连地球最基本的宜居性都无法捍卫，那它的优越性又从何谈起呢？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. So, we, I mean, we could go on this for a very long time, but I'm going to ask you instead about an episode in the book that in which you sort of have a fight with the editors of the FT over a single word, which appears in, you know, the signature phrase that Xi Jinping uses about the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, "minzu".
transcript.zh: 确实。这个话题我们可以聊很久，但我想换个角度，问问你书中提到的一个插曲。你曾因为一个词跟《金融时报》（FT）的编辑据理力争，这个词正是习近平的标志性话语“中华民族伟大复兴”里的“民族”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: This is a, not an easy word necessarily to translate. And we usually, I leave it in, in Chinese when I use it most of the time. But they insisted that it would be race. Give me the story in a minute, and tell me which, you know, which it was. Nobody on the desk could read the word, somebody could, but the scarier story somehow...
transcript.zh: 这个词其实并不好翻译。大多数时候提到它，我干脆就保留拼音。但他们却硬要把它译为“种族”（race）。你能不能简明扼要地讲讲当时是怎么回事？到底是因为编辑部里没人懂中文，还是有人懂，但出于某些博眼球的恐慌叙事而故意为之？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, so, so basically, I'm using that to illustrate a bias that I think creeps into the narrative perpetrated by the Western press. And I chose the FT because actually the FT is probably the most sensible paper out there. It's the most read, most influential.
transcript.zh: 对，我用这个例子其实是为了说明西方媒体叙事中潜移默化滋生的一种偏见。我之所以选《金融时报》，是因为它在业内恐怕算是最理性的报纸了，受众最广、影响力也最大。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And, and the reporting's, you know, generally the reporting's great. So, so I picked this particular episode just to illustrate it, because I had quite a long run-in with the Asia editor about 10 years ago. So, there were several articles that I objected to.
transcript.zh: 坦白讲，他们的报道大体上是很出色的。我特意挑这个插曲来说明问题，是因为大概十年前，我和他们的亚洲版主编有过一段相当旷日持久的交涉。当时有几篇文章的用词我实在无法苟同。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, anyway, the article was basically saying that Xi Jinping's slogan of the rejuvenation of the Chinese people, nation, was, should have been the Chinese race, and that it was revanchist and it had dark echoes of 20th century European history.
transcript.zh: 不管怎么说，那篇文章的大意是：习近平口中的“中华民族伟大复兴”，应该翻译成“中华种族”，并称这具有极强的复仇主义色彩，带着20世纪欧洲历史的阴暗回响。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, basically just, yeah, yeah, it's just basically saying it's Nazi. So, anyway, so I happened to be in London. So, I went along to the big Waterstones in Piccadilly, and I went upstairs and I looked, there were nine dictionaries, Chinese-English dictionaries, on the top floor.
transcript.zh: 直白点说，就是拐弯抹角地把这定性为纳粹主义。当时我碰巧在伦敦，就去了皮卡迪利大街上那家大型的水石书店（Waterstones）。我上到顶楼，翻遍了那里的九本汉英词典。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, I looked up all, all of them said that "minzu" meant nation, and none of them said it meant race. So, I sent this in to the FT and they said, "No, no, no, our translators say it means race." So, so then I wrote to eight professors, and five of them wrote back and said, "No, minzu means nation."
transcript.zh: 我一本一本查过去，每一本都清楚地写着“民族”的意思是“nation”（国家/民族），没有一本解释成“race”（种族）。我把证据发给《金融时报》，他们却回复说：“不不不，我们的翻译坚持认为这就是种族。”于是我又写信请教了八位教授，其中五位回信确认：“没错，‘民族’就是‘nation’。”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And one said, 'Oh, that's really interesting. I'll go off and research it,' and then didn't respond. And then, one of them, who's probably the guru on the whole area, who's written a book on the subject, said, 'Well, it can mean both, but the word race in, you know, in English is very pejorative, and actually...'
transcript.zh: 其中一位说：‘这非常有意思，我回去做些研究，’随后就没了下文。还有一位可以说是该领域泰斗级的人物，曾就此写过专著，他说：‘这个词确实两种含义都有，但英文中的 race 一词带有极强的贬义，实际上……’

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And there is a Chinese word for race.
transcript.zh: 而且中文里本身就有对应 race 的词。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, exactly, zhongzu. Yeah, exactly. So, that was another point. So anyway, I wrote back again to the FT with all this, you know, evidence, and they just, they just said, 'No. We think it means race, and that's that.'
transcript.zh: 没错，就是‘种族’。所以这也是关键的一点。总之，我拿着所有这些证据再次给《金融时报》回信，他们却只是简单回复：‘不，我们认为它就是种族的意思，事实就是如此。’

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, so, I thought, then I just left it. But then, two months later, this is why it's important, two months later, the James Trenchard Professor of International Relations at UCL wrote an article saying that Xi Jinping was morphing from Stalin to Hitler, and that the West had to confront China before it was too late.
transcript.zh: 所以我想了想，当时就没再深究。但两个月后——这就是为什么这件事至关重要——伦敦大学学院的詹姆斯·特伦查德国际关系讲席教授发表了一篇文章，称习近平正在从斯大林蜕变为希特勒，西方必须在为时已晚之前与中国对抗。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And it was a very, very hysterical article which drew on the FT source. And I just, I just, that was, that, you know, it's very, very dangerous to have this hysterical overreaction.
transcript.zh: 那是一篇极其歇斯底里的文章，引用的正是《金融时报》的这一说法。我当时就觉得，产生这种歇斯底里的过度反应是非常危险的。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, of course there are parts of the Chinese system that are, you know, very, very difficult for us to accept, or think that it is, you know, the right part, the right way to do things. So, that's fine. But, you know, it exists. We have to recognize it.
transcript.zh: 当然，中国体制中确实有一些方面让我们很难去接受，或者很难认同那是正确的做法。这无可厚非。但客观事实摆在那里，我们必须看清它。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But trying to make an analogy between Stalin, Xi Jinping, and then saying it's getting worse and it's going to Hitler, that just doesn't help anybody. It doesn't help anybody understand how to defend ourselves, or benefit from China's rise.
transcript.zh: 但试图将斯大林与习近平类比，随后又宣称情况在恶化并滑向希特勒，这对任何人都毫无益处。这既无助于我们理解如何捍卫自身利益，也无法让我们从中国的崛起中获益。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, not everyone goes leaping, you know, sort of into a violation of Godwin's Law in the first graph of an op-ed like that, but you've invented a unit of measure that sort of addresses the more typical way in which we kind of allow that moral panic or hysteria to creep in: the Woodward scale, named for Dame Barbara Woodward, who was Britain's ambassador to Beijing in the second half of the 2010s.
transcript.zh: 确实，并不是每个人都会像那样在专栏的第一段就直接触犯‘高德温法则’。但你发明了一个度量单位，用来衡量那种更常见的道德恐慌与歇斯底里情绪的滋生方式——也就是‘伍德沃德指数’。它是以2010年代后半期英国驻华大使芭芭拉·伍德沃德女爵命名的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Explain to the listeners what it measures, and tell me whether the readings have gotten sort of worse over the years you've been doing this, because you know, this idea, even if it was tongue-in-cheek to begin with, it really did resonate with me, and I've written about this same phenomenon, as you know.
transcript.zh: 给听众解释一下它衡量的是什么吧，并告诉我这些年来这一指数的读数是否在持续恶化。因为即便这个概念最初带有几分戏谑调侃，它确实深深引起了我的共鸣，如你所知，我也曾撰文讨论过同样的现象。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Right. So, um, I once heard Dame Barbara Woodward make a speech, and it just struck me as being very sensible, balanced, knowledgeable. I've seen her make a speech at Cambridge University in Chinese as well, so she really, you know, she knows the country and the civilization and the culture.
transcript.zh: 好的。我曾听过芭芭拉·伍德沃德女爵的一次演讲，当时我觉得她非常通情达理、客观平衡且学识渊博。我也曾见她在剑桥大学用中文发表演讲，所以她是真正了解这个国家、文明与文化的。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So she made a speech, and it consisted of two parts separated by the word 'but'. So it was, start off: China's lifted 800 million people out of absolute poverty, urbanization, no slums, electrification...
transcript.zh: 她的演讲由前后两部分组成，中间用一个‘但是’隔开。开头是：中国让八亿人摆脱了绝对贫困、推进了没有贫民窟的城市化、实现了全面电气化……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And you know, all these good things that, you know, increase in life expectancy, nutrition, all these objective measures about how successful China has been over the last few decades. And then there's the word "but".
transcript.zh: 以及所有这些好的方面，比如人均预期寿命的增长、营养水平的提高，所有这些衡量过去几十年中国有多成功的客观指标。但紧接着，就会出现一个“但是”。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Right. And then, of course, there're all the issues that are very, very difficult to deal with, you know, the lack of representation, lack of, you know, sort of different systems in judiciary. You know, we all know what they are. Xinjiang, all these, all these difficult issues.
transcript.zh: 没错。紧接着当然就是所有那些极其棘手的问题：缺乏代表性、司法体系缺乏独立性等等。我们都知道有哪些：新疆问题，以及所有这些复杂的难题。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So basically what I did is imagine that speech is ten minutes long. Where the word "but" occurs is like a measure of how positive or negative you are about China. So if the word "but" appears at, after one minute, so you got a minute's worth of positive and nine minutes of misery, then you're pretty negative about China.
transcript.zh: 所以我基本上是这么设想的：假设这篇演讲长达十分钟，那个“但是”出现的节点，就成了衡量你对中国持肯定还是否定态度的标尺。如果“但是”在第一分钟就出现了，也就是一分钟的好话加上九分钟的声讨，那显然你对中国的态度相当负面。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So I don't think anybody is at number nine on the Woodward scale. I think Xi Jinping is probably only at about seven on the Woodward scale. But I wanted to use that as kind of a, a measure of where people are. So there, there are UK politicians who are almost at zero on the Woodward scale.
transcript.zh: 我觉得在“伍德沃德量表”上没人能达到第9级。我想即便是习近平，大概也只能拿到7级左右。但我之所以用它，是想把它当作衡量人们立场的一种尺度。英国有些政客在伍德沃德量表上几乎就是0级。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But my basic argument is it doesn't matter where you are on the Woodward scale, we just have to get real about China. So you know, for the, so this program to get more education into the system in the UK and set up think tanks and all these other good things that we can do, it doesn't matter where you are on the Woodward scale, it should unite people at the opposite ends.
transcript.zh: 但我核心的观点是：无论你在伍德沃德量表上处于什么位置，我们都必须认清真实的中国。因此，无论是要在英国教育体系中普及涉华课程、设立智库，还是做其他我们能做的实事，无论你的立场如何，这项事业都应该把两极的人群团结起来。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So if you're very negative about China, you need to know more about it to defend yourself. You know, basic concepts of Sun Tzu's Art of War, "know yourself and know your enemy, and you'll survive a hundred battles". So that's the negative side.
transcript.zh: 如果你对中国极其反感，你就更需要了解它来保护自己。这就像《孙子兵法》里的基本概念：“知己知彼，百战不殆”。这是针对偏消极的一方。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: For positive people who want to cooperate, you'll be able to cooperate more effectively if you understand the way that China works. So it ought to unite the, doves and the hawks.
transcript.zh: 而对于想与中国合作的积极派，只有理解了中国的运作方式，合作才能更富成效。所以它本该成为弥合鸽派与鹰派的公约数。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: It ought to. But I, I just think it's just such a political hot potato, just like it was for Feng Guifen in the 1860s in China. It's such a hot potato that I think that there will be a, well, I mean there is a negative reaction.
transcript.zh: 确实理应如此。但我认为这完全成了一个政治烫手山芋，就像19世纪60年代冯桂芬在中国面临的处境一样。它太敏感了，所以我认为必然会引来——事实上已经招致了——强烈的反弹。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, there's a deep psychological resistance. It's quite natural to humans to do this, right? That's right.
transcript.zh: 是的，人们内心存在着深刻的心理抗拒。人类本能地会产生这种反应，对吧？确实如此。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, there's another version of the Woodward scale, the one in which you can measure, I suppose, how long the litany of Chinese perfidy that you first recite before saying anything good about China is. That's the one I probably encounter that one more often. "Before I say anything good, let me offer you this recitation of all the evil." Yeah, God.
transcript.zh: 伍德沃德量表其实还有另一个版本，也就是用来衡量：某人在夸中国之前，必须先冗长罗列多少条关于中国不守信义的罪状。我平时遇到的往往更多是这一种：“在夸它之前，容我先声讨一遍它的种种劣迹。”唉，天呐。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay, onto the Great Enterprise, finally. Take us to the beginning. When did you decide that an A-level unit was the answer to all these woes we've just described?
transcript.zh: 好了，终于要聊到这项“大业”了。带我们回到最初的起点吧：你究竟是何时认定，设立一门A-level科目才是化解我们刚才所说的所有这些困局的答案？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Okay. So, in 2006, I wrote a, um, op-ed...
transcript.zh: 好的。2006年的时候，我写了一篇专栏评论文章……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I wrote a piece together with a great friend of mine, Alistair Michie, about 20 years ago now, saying that the sole focus on language is not necessarily the right way to go.
transcript.zh: 大约20年前，我和一位挚友Alistair Michie合写过一篇文章，指出把全部精力单单放在语言教学上未必是正确的方向。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right.
transcript.zh: 对。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So it's 20 years. The basic issue is that Brits don't really study foreign languages. I don't know what the stats are in America, but...
transcript.zh: 转眼已经过去20年了。根本问题在于英国人其实并不怎么学外语。我不太清楚美国的数据，但……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Worse, I imagine.
transcript.zh: 恐怕更糟。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Right. In French and German, so in French, the number of people who do A-level, which is a crucial stage when you are between 16 and 18 in the UK, the number of people who are doing French A-level has fallen from 13,000 to around 6,000 over the last 12 to 13 years. It's the same in German; Spanish is flat for different reasons.
transcript.zh: 是的。在法语和德语方面，以法语为例，在英国16到18岁这一关键阶段报考A-level的人数，在过去12到13年间，从1.3万人腰斩到了约6000人。德语也是同样的情况；西班牙语人数虽持平，但原因各异。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And there's a similar story at GCSE. So the focus of trying to get people to learn Mandarin, which is the government focus, is trying to push water uphill.
transcript.zh: 在GCSE（普通中等教育证书考试）阶段也是同样的光景。因此，英国政府目前一味把重点放在让大家学普通话上，根本就是逆水行舟、徒劳无功。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. It's actually in the way of your great enterprise.
transcript.zh: 确实。这反而成了你这项宏伟“大业”的绊脚石。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, I will argue that it's complementary, actually. So my personal experience of learning a foreign language before I learned Mandarin was learning French at school.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我其实想说二者是相辅相成的。在我学普通话之前，我自己学外语的经历是在学校里学法语。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And we had these appalling textbooks of this incredibly boring family going on a boring holiday in a boring car along a completely straight, boring road where two boring children never complained about their parents not stopping for ice creams or anything else. And I just thought, 'Well, why am I learning this?'
transcript.zh: 我们用的是那些糟糕透顶的教材，里面讲着极度无聊的一家人，开着无聊的破车，沿着笔直单调的大马路去过无聊的假期，两个无趣的孩子甚至从不抱怨父母不停车买冰淇淋或别的东西。我当时就想：“我学这玩意儿到底图什么？”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And then, as soon as I went to France, I absolutely loved it. So then I had an impetus to learn it.
transcript.zh: 可后来我一去法国，就彻底爱上了那里。于是我便有了主动学习的内在动力。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So what I'm saying is that it's not cart before horse, whether you do the language or you understand the civilization. They're complementary to each other.
transcript.zh: 所以我的意思是，先学语言还是先了解文明，并没有所谓本末倒置的问题。它们本就是互补的。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So what I tried to do was to create an A-level modeled on the existing A-level in Classical Civilisation. In Classics, there are 6,000 graduates per annum in the UK; there are 300 in Chinese.
transcript.zh: 因此，我所尝试做的，就是参考现有的“古典文明”A-level课程，打造一套中国文明A-level。在古典学领域，英国每年有6000名毕业生；而中国学方向只有300人。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: There are 300 in any degree that has either the word 'China' or 'Chinese' in it. So it's quite often say, Chinese and French, or Chinese and business studies.
transcript.zh: 这300人还囊括了所有学位名称中带有“China”或“Chinese”的学生，其中通常还是中国学加法语，或者中国学加商科这类联合学位。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So we need to drastically increase that pool of knowledgeable people to inform government and the civil service about how to deal with this new challenge. So that's the basic premise.
transcript.zh: 因此，我们迫切需要大幅扩充真正懂中国的人才储备，以便为政府和公务员系统提供洞见，应对这一全新挑战。这就是最基本的出发点。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: The government set up a language program called Mandarin Excellence Programme, which is great. Fully support it, it's marvelous. But it's not enough, that's the point.
transcript.zh: 政府此前设立了一个名为“卓越汉语教学项目”（Mandarin Excellence Programme）的语言项目，这固然很好，我全力支持，太棒了。但问题在于，这远远不够。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So we've spent £26 million over the last 10 years, and it is just an objective fact that the number of people doing A-level Mandarin has gone from 3,000 to 3,000.
transcript.zh: 我们在过去10年里为此投入了2600万英镑，但客观事实摆在眼前：参加普通话A-level考试的人数始终在3000人上下原地踏步。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: ...to 1,600. It's just an objective fact.
transcript.zh: ……降到了1600人。这就是客观事实。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right.
transcript.zh: 对。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So it's not working, and all sorts of different reasons why it's not working. The numbers are better at GCSE, so it's gone from about 4,000 to 7,000 or something.
transcript.zh: 所以这条路走不通，原因也是多方面的。GCSE（中等教育普通证书）阶段的数据倒是好看一些，大概从4000人增加到了7000人左右。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: At GCSE, the numbers are better?
transcript.zh: GCSE阶段人数增加了？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, the numbers are better, sorry, at GCSE. So that's the exam at 16.
transcript.zh: 是的，抱歉，我是说在GCSE阶段人数更多，也就是16岁时考的那个。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, but if you drill down into those numbers, quite a lot of the increase is Cantonese. And that's because Britain gave extra visas to Hong Kong.
transcript.zh: 但是如果仔细剖析这些数据，就会发现大部分增幅其实来自讲粤语的学生。这是因为英国向香港发放了额外签证。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Hong Kong.
transcript.zh: 因为香港。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, so basically, I mean, you can make an argument—this is overly cynical and unfair, but I'm going to say it anyway—which is, you know, we've spent 26 million teaching Chinese people how to speak Chinese.
transcript.zh: 没错，所以基本上可以这么说——虽然这可能过于愤世嫉俗且有失公允，但我还是要说——我们花了2600万英镑去教华人怎么说中文。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, of course we haven't, because what actually happens is they just pitch up on the day and they get all the A's. That's the problem. So no sensible 16-year-old Brit, non-native speaking Brit, will ever do Mandarin A-level.
transcript.zh: 当然我们并不是真这么做的，因为实际情况是，母语学生考试那天直接去考就能包揽所有A。问题就在这里。所以任何理智的、非母语的16岁英国本土学生，都绝不会去选修中文A-level。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Because if you do Mandarin A-level, you're going to be competing with native speakers, they're going to get the A's, so that's suicidal for university entrance. So it's just a completely structural problem with going purely the Mandarin route.
transcript.zh: 因为如果你选了中文A-level，就要和母语者同台竞争，A都被他们拿走了，这对大学录取简直就是自杀行为。所以，单纯走普通话语言教学路线存在着彻底的结构性缺陷。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, layer on top of that another problem, which is in the last 10 years to 2006, there have been 10 Secretaries of State for Education and seven schools ministers. So it's just a complete merry-go-round.
transcript.zh: 除此之外，还有另一个问题：在截至2026年的过去十年里，换了十任教育大臣和七位主管学校事务的副大臣。这简直就是走马灯一样的旋转木马。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So trying to get a dialogue with the Department for Education is very difficult.
transcript.zh: 因此，想跟教育部开展持续对话极其困难。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, there was one, I mean, it was Nick Gibb, I think. He was conservative who ran the—he was schools minister for close to a decade, yeah. You got to him, but he said no. What was the reason he gave you?
transcript.zh: 不过有一个人任期很长，我想是Nick Gibb。他是保守党人，担任学校事务副大臣接近十年。你联系上他了，但他拒绝了。他给出的理由是什么？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: He said no because he thought it was competitive with the Mandarin Excellence Programme. But it's not, especially at A-level, because Mandarin Excellence Programme doesn't really cope with A-level at all.
transcript.zh: 他拒绝是因为他认为这会与“中文培优项目”（Mandarin Excellence Programme）构成竞争。但事实并非如此，尤其是在A-level阶段，因为中文培优项目根本无法覆盖A-level。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So what I want to do is, Mandarin Excellence Programme is fantastic up to 16. But pupils go from studying 9 to 11 subjects at the age of 16, in the UK system, they then go down to three. Nobody is going to study Mandarin.
transcript.zh: 我的想法是，中文培优项目在16岁之前确实非常出色。但英国体制下，学生在16岁时要从学习9到11门科目骤减到只修3门。没人会选中文。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right.
transcript.zh: 对。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But they might study Chinese Civilisation. And if they do that, that would keep the spark of interest alive in 14, 15, 16-year-olds across this bridge to 18, and then you get more people coming to university to study Chinese.
transcript.zh: 但他们可能会选修中国文明。如果他们选了，就能让这群14、15、16岁孩子心中的兴趣火苗延续下去，架起通往18岁的桥梁，这样未来就会有更多人进入大学去研究中国。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: To do Chinese studies, Area Studies, yeah.
transcript.zh: 去读中国研究、区域国别学，对。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Chinese studies, yeah. And this was tremendously supported by 10 vice chancellors of Britain's universities. I actually taught a module in a local sixth form, and the pupils seemed to enjoy it and like it.
transcript.zh: 去读中国研究，没错。这个构想得到了英国十所大学校长的全力支持。我其实还在当地的一所六年级学院（高中）试讲过一个单元，学生们看起来非常享受也很喜欢。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I went to see the chair of Britain's largest business by market cap...
transcript.zh: 我还去拜访了英国市值最高的大型企业的董事长……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Which is what?
transcript.zh: 哪家公司？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I probably shouldn't say which one it is, but it's—and it changes, so that's why I deliberately use that measure. So anyway, so I went to see the...
transcript.zh: 我大概不便透露具体是哪一家，不过排名经常变动，所以我才故意用这个指标来指代。总之，我去了……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: at the office of the chair of that company. And the same day he read my proposal, the same day the chairman of Britain's largest company wrote to the prime minister, saying, "We've got to do this." So that's the level of support I get in business and academia.
transcript.zh: 在那家公司董事长的办公室里。他读完我方案的当天，这位全英国最大公司的董事长就在当天致信首相，说：“我们必须做这件事。”这就是我在商界和学界得到的支持力度。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I definitely know that I can raise the money to fund it. We need 6 million pounds, so it doesn't even need taxpayers' money. But the civil service and the politicians will not do it. They won't do it.
transcript.zh: 我绝对清楚自己能筹集到所需资金。我们需要600万英镑，所以甚至不需要纳税人掏一分钱。但公务员体系和政客们就是不肯做。他们根本不愿推进。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And this culminated in a Curriculum and Assessment Review which was done last year. So it's only done about every 10 to 15 years, so this is a very thorough review of the British curriculum, basically starting from ground zero and building back up, you know, what should we do?
transcript.zh: 这种局面在去年进行的一项“课程与评估审查”中达到了顶点。这项审查大约每10到15年才进行一次，是对英国课程体系的一次极其彻底的审视，基本上是从零开始重新构建，探讨我们到底该学什么。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So the mid-level civil servants at the Department for Education contacted me and said, "You need to feed into this process." And I just said, "Oh, I just lost the will to live on this." And they said, "No, you've got to do it." And I said, "I just can't face it." So they said, "Right, we'll help you do it."
transcript.zh: 于是教育部的一些中层公务员联系我，说：“你必须参与到这个流程中来提交意见。”我直接说：“唉，我在这件事上真的已经心力交瘁了。”他们却说：“不行，你必须做。”我说：“我实在受不了再折腾了。”于是他们说：“好吧，我们帮你来做。”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So they got, bless them, they got onto a conference call, and they scoped it all out, they helped me write it, so I made a submission to the Curriculum and Assessment Review.
transcript.zh: 于是他们，真是谢天谢地，组织了一次电话会议，把整个框架梳理出来并协助我撰写，最终我向“课程与评估审查”提交了一份方案。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That, by the way, is included in the book, right?
transcript.zh: 顺便提一句，那份方案也收录在书里了，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah. And that had a covering letter from the chair and deputy chair of the Russell Group, which represents 20 top universities, the chair of Universities UK, the chair of three of Britain's biggest companies—probably shouldn't say which ones—and academics, vice-chancellors of various universities. A whole Rolodex of the great and good supporting this.
transcript.zh: 是的。那份方案还附有一封联名推荐信，署名者包括代表20所顶尖大学的罗素大学集团正副主席、英国大学联合会主席、英国三家最大公司的董事长——我可能不便透露具体是哪几家——以及学者和多所大学的校长。整个名流圈的显赫人物都在支持这门课。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So that goes in. Not a squeak, no reply whatsoever. And then the Curriculum and Assessment Review comes out in November of last year. The words "China", "India", "Korea", "Japan", and "globalization" do not appear once in the 272 pages.
transcript.zh: 方案交上去了，结果毫无动静，连句回复都没有。随后，审查报告在去年11月出炉。整整272页的报告里，“中国”、“印度”、“韩国”、“日本”和“全球化”这些词一次都没有出现。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: The word "Chinese" appears once at a footnote on page 87, saying that Chinese is more difficult to learn than French. But I already knew that. So it's just never going to happen.
transcript.zh: “中文”这个词仅在第87页的一处脚注中出现过一次，写着中文比法语更难学。但这我早就知道了。所以，这事根本不可能指望他们推进。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So I then had an encounter with the top civil servant in the Department for Education, and I tried to explain about the knowledge gap and starting off, you know, that the Chinese know more about us than we know about them. I could see that this wasn't making much progress.
transcript.zh: 后来我见到了教育部的最高级别公务员，我试图向他解释认知差距的问题，首先就提到中国人对我们的了解远多于我们对他们的了解。我看得出来这番话根本没引起什么共鸣。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So then I gave the example, "I'm sure you know that the study of some Shakespeare is compulsory in Chinese middle school. It's normally Romeo and Juliet, because that's kind of the least controversial one." So I explained that, and the response was, "Oh, yes, but that's just in the particular."
transcript.zh: 于是我举了个例子：“您肯定知道，在中国初中，学习莎士比亚的部分作品是必修的。通常是《罗密欧与朱丽叶》，因为这部作品最没有争议。”我解释了这一点，对方的回答却是：“哦，是的，但那不过是个案细节罢了。”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And I wasn't quite sure what that meant, but it didn't sound good. So I then persisted and said, "Well, you know..."
transcript.zh: 我不太确定这话到底是什么意思，但听起来显然不妙。于是我继续坚持，说道：“可是，您知道……”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: When Wen Jiabao came over to see David Cameron, he bought Adam Smith's book, blah blah blah, it wasn't Wealth of Nations and so on. And the official just repeated, "Yes, but that's in the particular."
transcript.zh: 温家宝来见戴维·卡梅伦时买了一本亚当·斯密的著作等等，不是《国富论》那本。而那位官员只是反复说：“对，但那是特例。”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So I think what that means is that's just a very narrow data point which obscures the wider picture. So basically, that is, you know, a palm in my face saying, "No, there isn't a knowledge gap."
transcript.zh: 我想他的意思是，这只是一个非常狭隘的单一论据，掩盖了更宏观的图景。所以说白了，这就像是直接伸手推我脸上，表示：“不，根本不存在什么认知鸿沟。”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Thereby proving conclusively that there is a knowledge gap, because a top civil servant in the Department for Education doesn't even know that there is a knowledge gap, and that's part of the knowledge gap.
transcript.zh: 但这恰恰无可辩驳地证明了认知鸿沟的存在。因为教育部的高级文官甚至都不知道存在这种鸿沟，而这种浑然不觉本身就是认知鸿沟的一部分。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah. It's a sort of Dunning-Kruger effect. You've put together a syllabus, though, and it's essentially classical civilization for China, right? Dream of the Red Chamber, Zhuangzi, the Taiping Rebellion.
transcript.zh: 是啊，这有点达克效应的意思了。不过你已经整理出了一套教学大纲，本质上就是针对中国的“古典文明”课程，对吧？包括《红楼梦》、庄子、太平天国运动。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: When you make the case in the Financial Times, it's Taiwan and TSMC. You quote the line that "grown-ups only learn things in a crisis." So is the crisis talk, is that for the ministers to hear?
transcript.zh: 你在《金融时报》撰文阐述理由时，提到的则是台湾和台积电。你引用了一句话说，“成年人只有在危机中才会吸取教训”。那么，谈论危机是为了说给那些大臣们听的吗？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, would you still want this A-level if China were no threat to anyone at all? I mean, just abstractly as a civilization we ought to understand?
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，即便中国对任何人都毫无威胁，你还会希望推行这门 A-level 课程吗？纯粹将其抽象地视为一个我们理应去了解的文明？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, I think that there's, there are all sorts of different reasons why I would hope that someone would want to study Chinese civilization as a young person. So it's mind-enhancing to understand a completely different system.
transcript.zh: 是的，我认为作为年轻人，希望去研习中国文明是有各种各样原因的。去理解一个截然不同的体系，本身就能拓宽心智。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: You know, I mean we study classical philosophy because the ethics are relevant, the historical analogies are relevant today, not because we face some existential crisis. So I think that like studying history or philosophy is mind-enhancing.
transcript.zh: 就像我们学习古典哲学，是因为其伦理思想具有现实意义，其历史隐喻在今天依然适用，而不是因为我们面临某种生存危机。所以我认为研习历史或哲学能启迪思维。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But there's also utility as well. So it doesn't matter what you want to be, if you want to be an architect, or an engineer, or a car salesman, or a pharmacological researcher, it doesn't matter what you want to do. If you've got an understanding of China, it's likely during a working lifetime that you'll have more opportunities if you understand China, just because of the way the global economy is.
transcript.zh: 但它同样具有实用价值。无论你将来想成为什么——建筑师、工程师、汽车销售员，还是药理学研究员——无论从事什么行业，只要你懂中国，在职业生涯中就很可能会获得更多机会，这仅仅是由全球经济格局所决定的。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So I think we should study it anyway. But the issue is that we haven't, we don't really have a sense of impending crisis. And of course, I don't want that. What I'm trying to do is say, "Why don't we study this and come up with a strategy?"
transcript.zh: 所以无论如何我们都应该去学习。但问题在于，我们并没有真正感受到那种迫在眉睫的危机感。当然，我也并不希望发生危机。我所努力争取的，是想说：“我们为什么不能去研究它，并制定出相应对策呢？”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Because there are endless reports about the situation we're in. So the government published a thorough defense review, and it said that China is our "epoch-defining, structural challenge" that manifests itself in every aspect of national and government life, okay? So if it's an epoch-defining...
transcript.zh: 因为关于我们当前处境的报告已经层出不穷了。政府发布了一份全面的国防评估报告，称中国构成了“划时代的、结构性的挑战”，渗透到国家与政府生活的方方面面。那么，既然它是一个划时代的……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Why aren't we trying to do something about coping with that? It's just completely inconsistent. So, for example, the Parliamentary Foreign Affairs Select Committee wrote another report.
transcript.zh: 我们为什么不想办法去应对呢？这完全是前后矛盾的。例如，英国议会下院外交事务特别委员会又写了一份报告。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: There are endless reports, almost every year. There's one that's just come from the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China. The Foreign Affairs Select Committee just said this sentence: 'We have not been able to find anybody in government who can articulate a policy on China.'
transcript.zh: 这类报告层出不穷，几乎每年都有。对华政策跨国议会联盟刚刚也出了一份。外交事务特别委员会在报告里直接写道：“我们在政府内部找不到任何一个人能够把对华政策阐述清楚。”

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: That's just not good enough. We've got to get over this. We can't just wait until, you know, something like AstraZeneca goes bust, or Volkswagen collapses, or Huawei suddenly creates a chip that just makes Nvidia obsolete. We can't wait until that happens.
transcript.zh: 这根本不可接受。我们必须克服这一点。我们不能总等到像阿斯利康破产、大众汽车倒闭，或者华为突然造出某种芯片直接让英伟达被淘汰，我们绝不能坐等这种局面发生。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, EV costs of power in Germany, huh? So, your Great Enterprise, as I've been calling it, is focused on the UK. What about us poor Americans? I mean, everything you said about the knowledge gap applies equally, if not greater, to the US.
transcript.zh: 是啊，德国电动车的电力成本等等，对吧？所以你这项被我称为“大业”的计划主要针对英国。那我们可怜的美国人呢？我是说，关于认知鸿沟的一切，在美中之间同样适用，甚至可能更严重。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I suppose the ratio of Spanish to Mandarin learners would be more excusable in the US than the ratio of French to Mandarin learners in England, but the gap is there.
