Is there an analogous sort of point of insertion for China knowledge, in your understanding? I mean, you have a daughter who went to university in America.
transcript.zh: 我想，在美国西语学习者与中文学习者的比例，比在英国法语与中文学习者的比例要情有可原一些，但鸿沟依然存在。依你之见，美国是否有类似的切入点来普及中国知识？我记得你的女儿也是在美国读的大学。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: That's right. So, I don't have the same grasp of how the system works in America, but America actually did make quite a lot of effort about 15 years ago in this area. There was quite a lot of government spending on the teaching of Mandarin.
transcript.zh: 没错。我对美国体制的具体运作方式了解不如英国深，但大约在15年前，美国确实在这方面下过很大功夫。当时政府投入了大量资金用于普通话教学。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I think that was moderately successful. There was a lot of exchange as well, which of course exchange is terribly important. People actually come to China and see what it's like. So that was a major focus of the American education system.
transcript.zh: 我认为那取得了一定的成功。当时也有大量的交流项目，而交流显然至关重要。大家能够亲自来到中国，亲眼看看这里是什么样子。这曾是美国教育系统的一大重心。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: What I would say is, I think that America has a richer pool of thought leaders and scholars about China. Britain does as well, but it's much more fragmented.
transcript.zh: 我想说的是，美国在涉及中国的思想领袖和学者储备方面更为丰厚。英国也有，但要零散得多。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: There are some centers in the US which I think can be really helpful for policymakers. So I would say that the knowledge gap between the US and China is not great, but it's not quite as dire as it is in the UK.
transcript.zh: 美国有一些研究中心，我认为能为政策制定者提供极大助益。因此我想说，美中之间的知识鸿沟虽然也不容乐观，但还没像英国那样严峻。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: France is probably ahead of the UK; Germany is definitely ahead of the UK. So that's my focus, obviously, because that's where I come from.
transcript.zh: 法国可能走在英国前面，德国则绝对领先于英国。所以我主要关注英国，显然因为那是我的祖国。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, it comes down to this, as with so many things: we have to just sort of touch people one at a time. And that's how I end up doing it, and I try to get in front of as many audiences as I can and impress upon the importance of this. But in those opportunities, we were chatting the other day and you said, sort of offhand, that if there were a hook, an historical epoch or an event that you would use to draw them in, it would be the Taiping Rebellion, or...
transcript.zh: 说到底，很多事情都是这样：我们只能一个人一个人地去触动。我最后也是这么做的，我尽量面对尽可能多的受众，向他们强调这件事的重要性。但在那些机会里，前几天我们聊天时你曾随口提到，如果要找一个引人入胜的切入点——一个历史时代或事件来吸引他们——那会是太平天国运动，或者……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The Taiping Civil War, as Stephen Platt now has me calling it, it's a great historical starting point to get a person interested in modern China. I'm sold on that idea, you needed only to say it and I saw exactly why. But walk our listeners through why it is such a compelling tale to get people into the door.
transcript.zh: 太平天国这一时期的内战——正如 Stephen Platt 让我改口称呼的那样——是让一个人对近现代中国产生兴趣的绝佳历史切入点。我完全认同这个观点，你只要一提我就立刻明白了缘由。不过，还是请你向我们的听众具体讲讲，为什么这是一个如此引人入胜、能吸引大家入门的故事？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Well, because it's just so vast and enormous and not really sort of something that we could think could possibly have happened, you know, 25 million deaths caused directly or indirectly, instigated by an uneducated civil, failed civil...
transcript.zh: 嗯，因为它的规模实在太浩大、太惊人了，而且几乎超出了我们认为可能发生的事情的范畴。你知道，直接或间接导致的死亡人数达2500万，而这一切竟是由一个没有受过良好教育的、落榜的文官……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, he wasn't uneducated, I mean he did take the exam four times. It was a tough exam, I don't think I would have passed it.
transcript.zh: 呃，他可不是没受过教育，我的意思是，他毕竟参加了四次科举考试。那可是非常难考的试，我觉得换了我肯定也考不过。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, but he failed it, and that's why he had that crisis. Okay, I'll take that back then, Kaiser, I'll take that back.
transcript.zh: 对，但他考砸了，这也正是他精神崩溃的原因。好吧，那我就收回刚才的话，Kaiser，我收回。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But the point is that he suffered a mental crisis, and he then latched on to biblical texts which were being supplied by missionaries in southern China, and he became convinced that he was the second son of God, the other brother of Jesus. And then set up this colossal rebellion, which went through the most extraordinary ups and downs: sieges, and ambushes on rivers, and this tremendous struggle by the Qing emperor to try and put it down.
transcript.zh: 但关键在于，他遭遇了严重的精神危机，随后抓住了当时华南传教士分发的圣经文本，并坚信自己是上帝的次子、耶稣的亲弟弟。接着他掀起了这场规模宏大的起义，其过程经历了极具戏剧性的跌宕起伏：围城、水路伏击，以及大清皇帝为平定叛乱而展开的惨烈搏杀。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: For 12 years.
transcript.zh: 持续了整整12年。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: 12 years, yeah. And then internal rebellions even within the Taipings. So I just think it's an enormous drama that isn't really known. It's just on a scale that is completely epic, even by the standards of the appalling problems, the appalling disasters and catastrophes of Europe, you know.
transcript.zh: 整整12年，是的。而且在太平天国内部甚至还爆发了内讧。所以我认为这是一出极其宏大的历史戏剧，却鲜为人知。它的体量是绝对史诗级的，即便是拿欧洲那些骇人听闻的灾难与浩劫标准来衡量，也是如此。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, I just think it's not really known, and I just think the sort of the images and strange, sort of mythical anecdotes that come out of that story would capture the imagination of a young person. I hope so, anyway.
transcript.zh: 所以，我觉得它确实不为人所熟知，而从那段历史中衍生出的种种画面感，以及那些怪诞、带有神话色彩的轶事，绝对能激发年轻人的想象力。至少我是这么希望的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah. So last year, as you say, in June, the Labor government published its China audit, and David Lammy, who was then the foreign secretary, stood up in Parliament and he admitted that Britain had a profound lack of knowledge of China's culture, history, language.
transcript.zh: 是啊，没错。正如你所说，去年6月工党政府发布了对华审查报告，时任外交大臣的 David Lammy 在议会站出来承认，英国对中国的文化、历史和语言极度匮乏了解。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Two months later, your op-ed ran. Three months after that, the Department of Education published this big review of the actual curriculum, 200 pages, and you said the word "China" didn't appear except "Chinese" in a footnote on page whatever.
transcript.zh: 两个月后，你的专栏文章刊发了。又过了三个月，教育部发布了一份厚达200页的课程审查重磅报告，而你说“中国”这个词甚至都没出现过，除了在某一页的脚注里提到了“中文”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Who in the system can actually say yes? Is there still a shot? You haven't given up, obviously. This is still something that you're passionate enough to spend this much time talking to me about, and you're going to self-publish a book, and have you been to see Georgia Gould, who's the relatively new minister for school standards, or...?
transcript.zh: 在这个体系中，到底谁能真正拍板同意？还有希望吗？显然你还没放弃。你对这件事依然充满热情，愿意花这么多时间跟我长谈，还要自费出书；那你去见过新任负责学校标准的部长 Georgia Gould 了吗，还是……？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Okay. So, there are pockets inside the government who understand this. And the places that I've found those pockets are in the Foreign Office, obviously, and the Cabinet Office. And it has to be a whole-of-government, because that's...
transcript.zh: 好的。其实在政府内部，有些部门是明白这一点的。据我所知，能理解此事的部门显然包括外交部，还有内阁办公厅。但这必须是一项全政府协同的工作，因为……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: That's the scale of the challenge. So, I think it has to be driven right from the top by the Cabinet Office.
transcript.zh: 这就是挑战的规模所在。因此，我认为这必须直接由最高层——也就是内阁办公厅来推动。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And that's that's full stop. It's not it's not just an issue of education, it's a change of mindset that will take decades to accomplish, just like it did with the Qing.
transcript.zh: 必须如此，毫无妥协余地。这不仅仅是一个教育问题，而是一种思维方式的转变，需要数十年才能完成，就像当年的清朝一样。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And there'll be all sorts of pushback, but we can learn so much by what the Qing did. As a result of Feng Guifen's essays, the government set up the Tongwen Guan, the School of Combined Learning.
transcript.zh: 期间会遇到各种各样的阻力，但我们可以从清朝的做法中汲取大量经验。正是因为冯桂芬的文章，清政府才设立了同文馆，即京师同文馆。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Which started off—this is very ironic, cause it started off with language. And then they realized language wasn't enough, so they started with maths and astronomy.
transcript.zh: 它最初——这非常有讽刺意味——是从语言教学起步的。随后他们意识到单学语言远远不够，于是开始教授算学和天文。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And then a guy translated a big text about international law, and then the Chinese mandarins then understood about the concept of sovereignty and fixed borders and so on, which had just completely alien to them.
transcript.zh: 接着有人翻译了一部关于国际法的大部头著作，中国官员们这才理解了主权和明确边界等概念，而这些在过去对他们来说完全是闻所未闻。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The Westphalian nation-state, right.
transcript.zh: 威斯特伐利亚主权国家体系，确实。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, exactly, yeah. So, I think we need to set up our own Tongwen Guan.
transcript.zh: 一点没错。所以，我认为我们需要建立我们自己的“同文馆”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And well, be prepared to be patient. I mean, Feng Guifen's essays circulated, as you said, in manuscript for decades before finally, you know, I mean, the Guangxu Emperor reads them in 1898 during the Hundred Days. That was a long time, 30 years, 40 years after.
transcript.zh: 而且，还得有足够的耐心。正如你所说，冯桂芬的文稿在民间以抄本形式流传了数十年，直到1898年百日维新期间光绪帝才读到。那已经过去了很久，是三四十年之后了。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, and there was endless pushback by the conservative faction in the court led by the Grand Chancellor, whatever he was called, Woren. And there are still preserved memorials going up to the emperor saying, why do we need to study mathematics? Why do we need to know about astronomy?
transcript.zh: 是的，朝廷里的保守派也进行了无休止的抵制，领头的是所谓大学士倭仁。现在还能看到保存下来的上奏折子，写着：我们为什么要学算学？为什么要懂天文？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: What we need to do is strengthen the ethical bases of the civil service on Confucian ethics. Yeah, sure, you need that, but you also need to understand maths.
transcript.zh: 我们真正需要做的是用儒家伦理来巩固文官体制的道德根基。没错，这些确实需要，但你也必须懂得数学。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. The title of your book, *Teach the People*, it comes from Guan Zhong, the statesman of the State of Qi in the 7th century BC in the Spring and Autumn period. If you, what does he say? If you...
transcript.zh: 对。你书的名字《教民》（Teach the People），出自公元前7世纪春秋时期齐国政治家管仲的名言。他是怎么说的来着？如果你……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Plan for a day, plant a seed. Sorry, plan for a year, plant a seed. Plan for 10 years, plant a tree. Plan for 100 years, teach the people.
transcript.zh: “一日之计，播之以谷”——不好意思，“一年之计，莫如树谷；十年之计，莫如树木；百年之计，莫如树人”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right, right, right. I've seen it rendered "cultivate," I think it's yǎng (养), right? But, you know, that's still a long time horizon for a policy campaign.
transcript.zh: 对对对。我见过有的地方译为“培育”，原文大概是“养”吧？不过，对一项政策倡议来说，这依然是一个极其漫长的时间跨度。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's also about the span from the founding of the Tongwen Guan in '62 to, you know, the fall of the dynasty 50 years later in 1912.
transcript.zh: 这差不多也是从1862年同文馆创立，到50年后1912年清朝覆灭的时间跨度。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, well, I've already spent 20 years on it. Yeah, it's a long time.
transcript.zh: 是啊，而我在这件事上已经耗费了二十年。确实是很长的一段时间。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah. Suppose you win, so the first cohort sits for this exam at the end of the decade, and by the 2040s, some of them are in the Foreign Office, in boardrooms, on, hopefully, in newsroom desks. Give me one decision that comes out differently because of it.
transcript.zh: 嗯。假设你成功了，第一批学生在这十年末参加了这项考试，到了2040年代，他们中的一些人进入了外交部、董事会，甚至有望进入新闻编辑室。请举出一个会因此而做出不同决定的例子。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What does a Britain that actually knows China do that the Britain of today can't?
transcript.zh: 一个真正了解中国的英国，能做到哪些当下的英国做不到的事？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Okay. So, one of the things that is really important is that...
transcript.zh: 好的。其中一件非常重要的事情在于……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: There is a total lack of transparency about what the government thinking is. So for example, you just mentioned the China audit last year that the Foreign Secretary announced, but that was then classified. So nobody knows what it says.
transcript.zh: 关于政府的真实想法，目前完全缺乏透明度。举例来说，你刚才提到外交大臣去年宣布的涉华审查，但随后它就被列为机密，因此没人知道具体内容。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, I think the lack of transparency is extremely damaging because it creates sort of suspicion and shadow boxing and all these other things. So one thing I think is really important is to get really clear guardrails where we're not going to cooperate, but we are going to cooperate, we're going to welcome things within that.
transcript.zh: 我认为缺乏透明度的危害极大，因为它滋生了猜忌、假想敌交锋以及诸如此类的事情。所以有一点非常重要：必须树立清晰的护栏——明确哪些领域绝不合作，但在护栏之内，我们既要开展合作，也要欢迎投资。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So that would be that would be one of the most basic decisions that I would hope would happen. So for example, you know, Mingyang was wanted to invest 1.5 billion pounds in a wind farm factory in Scotland, and the government banned it. So, but they haven't explained why.
transcript.zh: 这将是我希望看到的最基本的决断之一。例如，明阳智慧能源本想投资15亿英镑在苏格兰建一座风电制造厂，结果政府予以叫停，却从未说明背后的缘由。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So with Huawei, which was banned out of the UK telecom system, just a quick anecdote here. So I have a little flat in Cambridge, and it's between Magdalene College and Jesus College, next to Magdalene Bridge. There is no mobile signal there.
transcript.zh: 以被排除在英国电信系统之外的华为为例，我分享一个小插曲。我在剑桥有一间小公寓，位于麦格达伦学院和耶稣学院之间，紧挨着麦格达伦桥。在那里，手机完全没有信号。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So that's right in the center of a world-leading thought thought center, there's no signal, all right? At the end of the road, there's a pub called Byron's Bear, and until about 6 months ago there was no signal, and there was no fixed line internet.
transcript.zh: 这里可是在世界顶尖思想中心的腹地，居然连信号都没有，对吧？路尽头有一家叫 Byron's Bear 的酒吧，直到大约六个月前，那里不仅没信号，连有线宽带都没有。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Right in the center of Cambridge, and yet we banned Huawei. Okay. So, I I was...
transcript.zh: 就在剑桥的核心地段，可我们却禁用了华为。好吧，所以……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Were they at least, I mean the years ago they were in the 21st Century Network thing, that that project, they they had won some big bid and I mean, their having won ended up killing Marconi and I'm Do you remember this?
transcript.zh: 至少多年前他们曾参与过“21世纪网络”项目，中标了大单，而他们这一中标最终导致了马可尼公司的倒闭，你还记得这事吗？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I mean, I the the thing I've been focused on is that, Hua- Huawei was exclu- excluded from the network, and I was told by a very, very sen- basically the top person in the security service in the UK. I was personally told that they had a plan to deal with it.
transcript.zh: 我一直关注的是，华为被排斥在网络建设之外，而英国安全部门极高层的一位主管曾亲口告诉我，他们原本有一套成熟方案来应对相关问题。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: You know, they they they had a plan that they thought was would alleviate all the risks associated with Huawei, but foreign policy got involved because America, there's a lot of, you know, there's a lot of pressure from the States, yeah. So, so I think that, well, one of the things we need to be more transparent, and we need to openly discuss and then agree what the guardrails are.
transcript.zh: 他们本有一套自认为能消除所有与华为相关风险的方案，但外交政策横插了一脚——因为美国那边施加了极大的压力。因此，我认为我们需要提高透明度，公开讨论并敲定护栏究竟立在哪里。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: And that will be very difficult process because of the enormously different you know, views views on China. But, you know, if we seriously worried that you know, China's going to start hacking into our microwaves and fridges and turning them off, yeah, I mean, if if that could possibly ever be true, got a far bigger problem than just our fridges going down.
transcript.zh: 由于对华观点的巨大分歧，这必将是一个极其艰难的过程。但如果我们真的担心中国会黑进我们的微波炉和冰箱并远程切断电源——假如这种荒谬的事真会发生，那我们的麻烦可远比冰箱罢工大得多了。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: So, so we did we need to discuss that really basic thing: Where can we cooperate, and where do we need to be very defensive?
transcript.zh: 所以我们必须把这个最根本的问题摆上台面：在哪些领域我们可以合作，又在哪些领域必须严加防范？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, Tim, I I will continue to pump...
transcript.zh: 好的，Tim，我还会继续去推……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: For your your great enterprise and and uh, I think it's been it's it's really inspiring. And the the book is terrific. I think that anyone would enjoy reading it. It's so so enjoyably written, and the syllabus itself is really it's great.
transcript.zh: 为了你的这项大业。我认为这真的非常鼓舞人心。而且这本书写得太棒了，我觉得任何人读起来都会觉得津津有味。文笔极具可读性，而且课程大纲本身也非常出色。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's it's it's revisiting my old education. And I feel like you've done an excellent job in putting together that syllabus. I think many generations of students will thank you for leaving out Song Neo-Confucianism.
transcript.zh: 它让我重温了自己当年的求学生涯。我觉得你在编纂这份大纲方面做得极其出色。我想未来几代学生都会感谢你没有把宋代理学塞进去。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yes, I think so, yeah. There's modern bits in there as well, so like, you know, Reform and Opening Up. So it's not just Taiping and Confucius.
transcript.zh: 是的，我也这么觉得。里面也包含不少现代内容，比如改革开放。所以并不全是太平天国和孔子。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, I look forward to the publication of the book, and I'll make sure to make an announcement here on the pod when when that happens. So now, onto the segment that I call "paying it forward," where I ask the guest to name check one individual, generally a younger person, who's doing great work that's deserving of recognition.
transcript.zh: 我很期待这本书的正式出版，届时我一定会在播客里向大家推荐。那么接下来进入我们“薪火相传”的荐人环节，我会请嘉宾推荐一位通常是后起之秀的青年才俊，他正在从事非常出色且值得被关注的工作。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Someone in your orbit, Tim, or in your area of work ideally. Who do you have for us?
transcript.zh: 最好是你身边认识的人，Tim，或者是在你所属工作领域里的。你今天想推荐谁？

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Okay, so I'm going to nominate Morrison Cleaver. At the CBBC. Because he's a trailblazer...
transcript.zh: 好的，我想推荐 Morrison Cleaver。他在英中贸易协会（CBBC）工作。因为他是一位开拓者……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The Children's BBC? No.
transcript.zh: 儿童版的 BBC（CBBC）？不是吧。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, no, not quite. So, no, because he's a trailblazer, and he's enthusiastic, and you know, very open-minded, knowledgeable, one of the few people that actually did study Chinese at university.
transcript.zh: 哈哈，不是那个。我想推荐他，是因为他极具开拓精神、充满热情，而且思想非常开放、知识渊博，是大学里真正主修中文的少数人之一。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: I think he told me, at Cambridge, I think he told me that there were about 10 people. But he's, you know, very resourceful, very energetic, and he's a trailblazer, and he's still in his 20s. So, I wish him the absolute best.
transcript.zh: 他在剑桥念书时，好像跟我说过他们那一届只有大概十个人。但他非常有谋略，充满干劲，敢为人先，而且才二十多岁。我由衷地祝愿他前程似锦。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, Yenching Scholar. I actually tweeted one day, because it was funny, I rolled up to my favorite watering hole, The Golden Weasel, and there he was sitting on the stoop along with two other Europeans. They were attentively watching something on a phone.
transcript.zh: 没错，他还是燕京学者。有一天我还发了条推文，因为实在太逗了，我溜达到我最喜欢的常去酒吧“金鼬”，正巧看见他和另外两个欧洲人坐在门前台阶上。他们正目不转睛地盯着手机看什么东西。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It turned out they were watching the EU Trade Commissioner's speech and press conference at a bar in Beijing of an evening. That's, it's one of those "only at The Golden Weasel" moments.
transcript.zh: 结果一问才发现，他们竟然在北京一家酒吧的傍晚时分，聚精会神地看欧盟贸易专员的演讲和新闻发布会。这真是典型的“唯有在金鼬才会发生”的名场面。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: That's dedication for you.
transcript.zh: 这就叫敬业精神。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, a great guy. And he was he's the one who lent me a copy of your book so that I was able to read it ahead of this, so fantastic, great one. Now onto recommendations where I ask for, you know, a novel or a film or a piece of music or a travel destination, something you've enjoyed.
transcript.zh: 是啊，非常棒的一个人。正是他借给了我你那本书的试读本，我才能在这次录制前读完，所以太棒了，推荐得好。现在进入我们的常规推荐环节，通常会请嘉宾推荐一本小说、一部电影、一首乐曲或者一个旅行目的地，任何你最近很享受的事物都可以。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yeah, so we we were chatting about this earlier, and so so I've actually been reading fiction recently, more more than, you know, tomes about China, which are which are great anyway. So so I I mentioned to you that I I've read Middlemarch for the first time just recently, which I I just absolutely loved it.
transcript.zh: 是的，我们之前也聊过这个话题。其实我最近读了不少虚构类小说，看得比那些关于中国的大部头还要多——虽然那些学术专著也都很精彩。我之前跟你提过，我最近生平第一次读了《米德尔马契》（Middlemarch），简直是爱不释手。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: But if if I'm going to do anything, I'm going to recommend Bleak House, which is the Dickens story about an interminable lawsuit that goes on generation after generation and never, ever gets solved. And the legal fees ruin both the plaintiff and the defendant. And it's extremely funny. And it's written in a way that's it's not...
transcript.zh: 但如果要推荐一部作品，我还是想推荐《荒凉山庄》（Bleak House）。这是狄更斯写的一部小说，讲的是一场耗费数代人光阴、却永远无法结案的冗长诉讼。高昂的诉讼费把原告和被告都搞得倾家荡产。这部书极其诙谐幽默，而且它的写作笔法让人觉得……

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Terribly easy to understand, but I think that's the joke on us. I think that Dickens wrote the novel in a way that the lawsuit was being presented, so it's just completely basically completely incomprehensible. But highly entertaining as you go through it.
transcript.zh: 非常容易理解，但我认为这正是他在同我们开的玩笑。狄更斯是以那场诉讼展现的方式来写这部小说的，所以本质上完全晦涩难懂。但读起来却极具趣味性。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, you know, that's one Dickens work I've not yet read, but it's the second time that somebody's recommended it on this show, so I will get to that, and it goes right to the top of the list. Middlemarch still is one of my my all-time favorite novels, and and, yeah, I will al- always, you know, get a plug in for that. Reading Middlemarch again and again is is always worthwhile, thoroughly rewarding.
transcript.zh: 狄更斯的这部作品我确实还没读过，但这是第二次有人在节目里推荐它了，我一定会去读，直接把它列到书单最前面。《米德尔马契》依然是我有生以来最喜欢的小说之一，是的，我无论何时都会顺便安利它。一遍又一遍地重读《米德尔马契》绝对是值得的，会带来莫大的收获。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's it's funny, you know, it shows up in in other places in popular culture. The uh the the odious husband who's writing a book called The Key to All Mythologies—Casaubon.
transcript.zh: 很有意思的是，它还经常出现在流行文化中的其他地方。那个令人讨厌的丈夫，正在写一本名为《开启万种神话之钥》的书——卡苏朋。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Yes. Casaubon.
transcript.zh: 是的，卡苏朋。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, Casaubon. He's he's uh writing this book called The Key to All Mythologies, which is the name of the trilogy that Jonathan Franzen is now writing. It's it's he's calling it The Key to All Mythologies in an obvious reference. Yeah.
transcript.zh: 没错，卡苏朋。他当时在写一本叫《开启万种神话之钥》的书，而这正好是乔纳森·弗兰岑目前正在创作的三部曲的名字。他把它叫做《开启万种神话之钥》，显然是对前者的致敬。是的。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Oh, right. Marvelous.
transcript.zh: 噢，原来如此。太妙了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay, my recommendation this week: so two novels by the the writer Mohsin Hamid, who I'm happy to say has kind of become a friend. We've both been part of this Georgetown Global Dialogues series of conferences that just wrapped up. In the last couple of gatherings, we really hit it off.
transcript.zh: 好了，我这周的推荐是：作家莫辛·哈米德的两部小说。很高兴地说，他如今也算是我的朋友了。我们俩都参加了刚刚结束的乔治城全球对话系列研讨会。在过去几次聚会中，我们非常投缘。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He he was, I guess supposed, curious, in the way that a novelist is curious, about why, as an American, I would pack up and move to China. He One of his books is sort of about exiting the United States. He He's the author of this book called The Reluctant Fundamentalist. He's the one who put it in my hands first, so um I told him I'd never read it, it which is a little embarrassing to admit for a book that's, you know, been out for 20 years and it, you know, got quite a bit of press.
transcript.zh: 我想，他带着小说家特有的好奇心，想弄明白为什么我作为一个美国人会收拾行囊搬去中国。他的其中一本书某种程度上就是关于离开美国的。他写过一本叫《拉合尔茶馆的陌生人》的书。是他亲手把这本书交给我的，所以我告诉他我以前从未读过——承认这一点确实有点尴尬，毕竟这本书已经出版了二十年，而且当年大受媒体关注。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You can read it in a sitting. It's it's quite short, and it's told entirely as one side of a conversation between a young Pakistani man, a Princeton-educated guy, formerly a rising star in a New York valuation firm—I mean, it's semi-autobiographical, he worked at McKinsey, he went to Princeton, he went to Harvard Law. And he sits an American down at a cafe and and and and monologues at him. It's sort of a second-person novel, sitting in Lahore, and um walks him through a whole evening and and and a night.
transcript.zh: 你一口气就能读完它。篇幅很短，通篇以独白的形式展开，记录了一个年轻巴基斯坦男人的单向对话。他毕业于普林斯顿，曾是纽约一家资产评估公司的后起之秀——某种程度上带点半自传色彩，作者本人曾在麦肯锡工作，上过普林斯顿和哈佛法学院。他让一个美国人在拉合尔的一家咖啡馆坐下，对着他滔滔不绝地倾诉。这算是一部第二人称视角的小说，两人坐在拉合尔，走过了一整晚的时光。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You never hear the American guy speak. And that's sort of the whole trick of the thing, cuz the book is about a man who really understands America very intimately: its schools, its firms, its whole courtship rituals. There's a lot of stuff that sort of on the nose. The firm he works for is called Underwood Samson, U.S. The woman he dates is named Erica, as in, um, America.
transcript.zh: 你自始至终听不到那个美国人开口。这也正是这部作品的精妙之处，因为整本书讲述的是一个对美国有着极其透彻了解的人：那里的学校、企业，乃至整套求偶仪式。书里很多隐喻都直白得恰到好处。他工作的公司名叫安德伍德·萨姆森（Underwood Samson），缩写就是U.S.；他约会的女人名叫艾莉卡（Erica），暗合阿美莉卡（Am-Erica）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And, you know, they they they there's a lot of, you know, quite deliberate, sort of on the nose symbolism. But, yeah, it the ending is just really, it's great, it's great. The other the other one that I read right after that is called Exit West, which is a very different book, in some ways kind of a maybe a braver one, I don't know. I mean, they're both very brave. It's about a young couple
transcript.zh: 书里有很多非常刻意且直白的象征隐喻。但是，结尾真的非常精彩，非常棒。读完那本之后我紧接着读的另一本叫《离开西方》，那是一部截然不同的作品，在某些方面甚至更具勇气，我也不好说，其实两部都极有胆识。它讲述了一对年轻夫妇的故事，

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...from a city that's coming apart. It sort of feels like, you know, Damascus or something. I'm going to guess from various clues that it's a Syrian city. And it's about the refugee, the migrant experience.
transcript.zh: ……来自一座正在分崩离析的城市。感觉有点像大马士革之类的地方。从各种线索来看，我推测那是一座叙利亚城市。它讲述的是难民与移民的经历。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And you know, it takes place all over the world. I mean, Mykonos, where they end up first, and then in London, and then in Marin County in California, but a very unrecognizable Marin. It's weird. We usually ask people about the stories of their migration, but in this, the conceit is that these weird sort of dimensional doors open up all over the place, and people just sort of walk through and end up on Mykonos, or walk through and end up squatting in a flat in North London.
transcript.zh: 而且，这个故事发生在世界各地。我是说，他们先是到了米科诺斯岛，然后到了伦敦，接着又到了加州的马林县，不过是一个让人完全认不出来的马林县。这很离奇。我们通常会询问人们关于迁徙的故事，但在这本书里，核心设定是世界各地都打开了奇特的维度之门，人们只要穿过去，就可能置身米科诺斯岛，或者穿过去就成了北伦敦某套公寓里的占屋寄宿者。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But it's great. It's also very much on the short side. It was shortlisted for the Booker, I think.
transcript.zh: 但这本小说很精彩，篇幅也很短小。我记得它还入围了布克奖的决选名单。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And this guy, Mohsin Hamid, he's just a delight. If you can hear him speak publicly, do it. He's just so wise and articulate.
transcript.zh: 而且作者 Mohsin Hamid 本人也非常有魅力。如果你有机会听他的公开演讲，一定要去。他非常睿智且表达精妙。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Of an evening, he sold me on the virtues—we were talking about Shanghai and Beijing, and why my preference is for Beijing. And then I was asking him about Pakistani cities that he's lived in, and he sold me on the virtues of Lahore, which now sounds a lot like Beijing: the place where you'll roll up to the bar and see people watching the European trade commissioner on TV without sound.
transcript.zh: 某天晚上，我们聊起上海和北京，以及为什么我更偏爱北京，他就向我极力推介拉合尔的好处。当时我向他打听他住过的巴基斯坦城市，他就向我盛赞拉合尔的种种妙处，如今听起来它和北京颇为相似——走进一家酒吧，会看到人们正看着电视上静音播放的欧盟贸易专员讲话。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, Mohsin, if you're listening, thank you. I owe you a Chinese novel in return. Tim Clissold, thank you so much for making the time and inviting me here to talk to you.
transcript.zh: 所以，Mohsin，如果你在收听的话，谢谢你。作为回报，我欠你一本中国小说。Tim Clissold，非常感谢你抽身相见，并邀请我来这里和你交谈。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Thank you. Thank you, Kaiser.
transcript.zh: 谢谢。谢谢你，Kaiser。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, it's been a real pleasure, and good luck with the Great Enterprise.
transcript.zh: 是的，非常荣幸。祝你的“大业”一切顺利。

transcript.speaker: Tim Clissold
transcript.en: Thank you.
transcript.zh: 谢谢。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You've been listening to the Sinica Podcast. The show is produced, recorded, engineered, edited, and mastered by me, Kaiser Kuo. Support the show through Substack at sinicapodcast.com, where you will find a growing offering of terrific original China-related writing and audio. Email me at sinicapod@gmail.com if you've got ideas on how you can help out with the show. Don't forget to leave a review on Apple Podcasts. Huge thanks to my guest, Tim Clissold, 'Mr. China' himself. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you next week. Take care.
transcript.zh: 您收听的是 Sinica Podcast。本节目由我 Kaiser Kuo 制作、录音、工程、剪辑并完成母带处理。欢迎通过 Substack 平台访问 sinicapodcast.com 支持本节目，在那里您可以获取越来越多优质的涉华原创图文及音频内容。如果您对协助节目的发展有任何想法，欢迎发邮件至 sinicapod@gmail.com。别忘了在 Apple Podcasts 上留下好评。非常感谢今天的嘉宾，《中国通》的作者 Tim Clissold 本人。感谢收听，我们下周再见，保重。
